The proposed approach offers significant practical advantages through its single-point boundary implementation, fast response, and robust full-body stabilization. Owing to these features, it holds strong potential for aerospace applications such as aircraft wings, deployable booms, and lightweight space structures, where effective vibration suppression is critical for operational reliability. This work marks a substantial advancement beyond existing boundary control techniques.

title: Innovative Y-shaped hydrogel mitral clip with magnetic actuation and hydrophilic janus surface for enhanced valve leaflet repair
abstract: We developed a magnetically responsive Y-shaped hydrogel mitral clip for minimally invasive repair of mitral regurgitation. Fabricated through a multilayer assembly strategy, the clip integrates a polyurethane layer featuring a biomimetic inverse opal architecture to enhance tissue adhesion, a GelMA/Fe3O4 hydrogel for magnetic actuation, a flexible epoxy acrylate scaffold for mechanical compliance, and a biocompatible polydimethylsiloxane interface. The clip exhibits Janus wettability, with a hydrophilic inner surface to promote effective leaflet anchoring and a hydrophobic outer surface to minimize blood fouling, thus optimizing device-tissue and device-fluid interactions. Performance was validated through in vitro, ex vivo, and computational studies, confirming precise magnetic clamping, strong adhesion, and mechanical resilience under simulated physiological conditions. Hemocompatibility evaluations demonstrated favorable outcomes in terms of blood interaction and reduced thrombogenicity when benchmarked against commercial alternatives. This soft, adaptive device supports minimally invasive deployment and reliable leaflet fixation, offering a promising approach for next-generation transcatheter mitral valve repair with enhanced tissue integration and blood compatibility.

title: Dynamic control of cantilever bistable composites: Theory and experiment
venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation
abstract: Bistable composite laminates, capable of maintaining two stable configurations without continuous energy input, are promising candidates for morphing aerospace structures. This study investigates the nonlinear dynamic behavior of cantilevered bistable composite plates and proposes a resonance-based actuation strategy for efficient configuration switching. A nonlinear dynamic model is developed based on Hamilton’s principle and the Rayleigh–Ritz method to accurately model nonlinear dynamic behavior of bistable plates. The dynamic characteristics under varying excitation amplitudes are analyzed through bifurcation diagrams, time histories, phase portraits, and Poincaré maps, revealing the evolution from periodic oscillations to period-doubling bifurcations, chaotic motion, and eventually snap-through. As the excitation frequency approaches the modal frequency, the vibration amplitude increases significantly. When the excitation amplitude exceeds a critical threshold, snap-through occurs, accompanied by the structure switching from one stable state to another. The theoretical predictions show good agreement with the experimental observations. The proposed resonance-based strategy enables rapid and energy-efficient configuration switching, providing practical insights for morphing structure design.

title: Pneumatic smart textile actuation
abstract: Textiles are lightweight, breathable, and soft, characteristics that make them naturally suitable platforms for wearable systems. Next-generation wearables that can change shape or generate interactive forces require the integration of soft actuators. Among them, soft pneumatic actuators are particularly promising because of their safety, relatively strong output forces, and rapid deformation. This review focuses on textile-based soft pneumatic actuators, also known as pneumatic textile actuators (PTAs), and their wearable applications. We summarize the design strategies and characteristics of PTAs from the perspective of actuation mechanisms, and we discuss textile material selection and related manufacturing processes. We also review soft sensors integrated with PTAs to enhance the intelligent perception of wearable devices. With the rapid development of PTA-based wearables, representative applications such as haptic displays, medical rehabilitation, and physical assistance have been introduced. Finally, future PTA-based smart wearables are expected to evolve toward multifunctionality, high integration, rapid customization, and environmental adaptability.

title: Sensor-actuator integration in intelligent devices: from functional synergy to emerging application
abstract: The integration of sensors and actuators in intelligent devices has led to the revolutionary change in the fields of robotics, healthcare, and IoT to allow the perception-to-action cycles. This interactions leads to real-time responsiveness, flexibility, and autonomy, and creates innovations, including soft robotics, bioelectronic medicine, and smart wearable devices. However, there are still problems associated with the attainment of signal coordination control, miniaturization and strong interoperability in dynamic environments. This paper reviews the design principles of sensor-actuator integration, highlighting key mechanisms for functional synergy, such as feedback architectures, multimodal sensing, and adaptive actuation. The emerging applications, including soft robotics and human-machine interfaces are then examined, with an emphasis on how cross-disciplinary solutions are tackling the existing constraints. Finally, we discuss the directions of the future, such as biohybrid systems and neuromorphic engineering, which are projected to restructure the limits of intelligent devices. By synthesizing theoretical insights with practical advancements, this work is expected to help the researchers overcome the existing limitations and open the opportunities of this rapidly evolving field.

title: Advancements and challenges of high-speed active flow control: Plasma actuators
venue: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer
abstract: Effective active flow control is crucial for high-speed aircraft to reduce drag, enhance heat dissipation, and improve fuel mixing characteristics. Plasma actuators, which offer rapid response times, lack of mechanical moving parts, and a broad operating frequency range, have emerged as a promising solution for these challenges. It has received extensive attention in the past 30 years. This review synthesizes findings from over 2700 relevant studies and over 300 in-depth papers on the application of plasma actuators in high-speed active flow control. The paper compares the technical features of various plasma actuator designs and examines their mechanisms for controlling high-speed flow fields, particularly focusing on shock wave control and boundary layer interference. Despite notable progress, challenges remain in fully leveraging the potential of plasma actuators for efficient flow control in high-speed aircraft. Nonetheless, advancements in plasma actuator technology hold the potential to revolutionize aircraft design and performance, marking a significant step forward in high-speed fluid mechanics.

title: Frequency–time domain method for an unrestrained aeroservoelastic system with actuator nonlinearities
venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation
abstract: The frequency–time domain method is an intriguing tool for analyzing nonlinear aeroelastic systems. However, the applications for closed-loop systems with actuator nonlinearities are challenging to implement; existing procedures require variable augmentation associated with control systems, which complicates the dynamic equations. To address these issues, this paper describes modifications to reconstruct nonlinear closed-loop systems. Nonlinear elements are disconnected at specific locations, whereas the remaining components are reorganized as frequency-domain blocks to obtain linear and impulse responses. Subsequently, a convolution integral is applied in the time domain to introduce the effects of nonlinearities into the outputs of nonlinear actuators. This hybrid frequency–time domain framework exhibits responses with various nonlinearities, leveraging both the frequency- and time-domain characteristics. Based on an unrestrained airfoil section, a closed-loop system with freeplay and actuator saturation is provided as a numerical example. Linear and nonlinear time responses induced by external excitation and initial conditions are calculated, validating the feasibility and accuracy of the proposed method. Furthermore, nonlinear frequency responses are directly obtained without additional operations. Notably, the proposed method enables efficient computations, reducing the computational time by an order of magnitude. This advantage scales effectively for advanced applications, for instance, uncertainty analysis. The introduction of unsteady aerodynamics is explored in the frequency domain to circumvent conventional approximation techniques, extending the applications of the frequency–time domain method.

title: Uncertainty-aware digital twins for safe operation and active fault-tolerance in degrading heterogeneous pumping systems
abstract: Conventional deterministic controls often fail in fluid systems under mechanical degradation due to epistemic uncertainties, leading to constraint violations. While passive fault diagnosis has advanced, autonomous risk-averse decision-making post-degradation remains lacking. To bridge this gap, this study proposes an Adaptive Probabilistic Digital Twin (APDT) framework. Utilizing Uncertainty Quantification (UQ), the APDT establishes mathematical guardrails based on the Probability of Feasibility, actively preventing physical boundary violations under deep uncertainties. Furthermore, the framework dynamically reconstructs system mappings online to adapt to non-stationary asymmetrical degradation, overcoming the limitations of static models. An embedded Trust-Region mechanism ensures smooth state transitions by preventing actuator fatigue. Crucially, trajectory analysis reveals an emergent “strategic offloading” behavior: the APDT autonomously shifts operational loads from degraded to healthy units. This acts as an active fault-tolerant mechanism, mitigating stress on deteriorating components to prevent sudden failures while maintaining robust output. Ultimately, the APDT offers a reliable, physics-compliant paradigm for the active safety management and life-extension of cyber-physical systems.

title: Design of hybrid actuation piezoelectric MEMS scanning mirror with reduced nonlinearity
abstract: MEMS scanning mirrors are compact, high-frequency devices widely used for precise light steering in applications such as image projection. However, conventional piezoelectric MEMS scanners often exhibit nonlinear behavior that distorts images and limits system performance. This study presents a novel hybrid-actuator design that integrates a normal force actuator and a transmission spring with a traditional clamped-clamped torsional actuator to reduce nonlinearity while enhancing the scanning angle. Finite element simulations were conducted to analyze the dynamic behavior and stress distribution of the design, followed by device fabrication on SOI wafers incorporating a KNN piezoelectric film. Experimental measurements demonstrate that the hybrid-actuator design effectively reduces nonlinearity, achieving a 44.6 % increase in scanning angle and producing significantly clearer projected images compared to conventional designs. Additionally, Fast Fourier Transform analysis of vibration signals revealed a substantial reduction in Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), decreasing from 43.8 % in the reference design to 14.8 % in the proposed design. This reduction in THD directly contributes to the mitigation of image blurriness, further highlighting the superior performance of the proposed scanner.

title: Conventional and additive manufacturing of NiTi shape memory alloy tubes: A review of fabrication, multiaxial thermomechanical behavior, constitutive modeling, and emerging applications in actuation and elastocaloric cooling
abstract: This review critically assesses the state of research on NiTi shape memory alloy tubes fabricated via both conventional thermomechanical processing and additive manufacturing (AM), with emphasis on Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF). Synthesizing over 157 studies on fabrication, multiaxial thermomechanical characterization, constitutive modeling, and applications in actuation and elastocaloric cooling, this work addresses the full lifecycle of NiTi tubes from processing to performance. Unlike prior reviews that treat AM fabrication or constitutive modeling of NiTi independently, this review integrates, for thin-walled tubular geometries specifically, fabrication-induced microstructure, multiaxial thermomechanical characterization, constitutive model validation, and application performance in a single treatment, a combination not addressed collectively by any prior review in this domain. Experiments under uniaxial tension, pure torsion, and proportional and non-proportional axial-torsional loading reveal significant tension-torsion coupling, rate-dependent transformations, and pronounced anisotropy in drawn tubes. A microplane-based constitutive model, validated against these experiments with a maximum error of 3.3%, effectively captures superelasticity and shape memory behavior across all loading paths. For LPBF-fabricated tubes, the review examines the influence of post-processing on transformation temperatures, strain localization, cyclic stability, and wall thickness effects, demonstrating that optimized heat treatment yields recoverable strains approaching those of wrought material. The analysis identifies four prioritized research gaps: (i) scarce multiaxial fatigue data for LPBF tubes, (ii) insufficient incorporation of AM-induced microstructural variability into constitutive models, (iii) the lack of standardized protocols for comparing conventional and AM tube performance, and (iv) limited integration of data-driven and machine learning methods with physics-based models for predictive design. A research roadmap is proposed, emphasizing manufacturing-aware models, LPBF-specific multiaxial datasets, and data-driven approaches to accelerate the translation of NiTi tubes into reliable engineering devices.

title: Actuation strategies and applications for high-output power soft robots
abstract: Recent breakthroughs in soft robotics have enabled transformative applications in manipulation, surgery, rehabilitation, and confined space exploration, driven by versatile smart materials that sense and respond to optical, thermal, electrical, and chemical stimuli. However, output power remains constrained by limited energy storage, delayed responses, and considerable dissipation. This review systematically examines the core design principles for agile locomotion, identifying three key strategies for high-output power through power amplification (PA): 1) increasing effective energy storage, 2) improving energy conversion efficiency by constraining losses, and 3) reducing energy release duration with latching mechanisms. By surveying representative examples across terrestrial, aerial, and aquatic environments, this work outlines key challenges and future directions to advance next-generation, high-output power soft robots. These insights lay a foundational framework to guide future innovations in soft robotics where enhanced actuation strength, speed, and functionality are essential.

title: Interaction between external forcing modes and self-excited thermoacoustic modes in a single-element liquid rocket engine: Bifurcation routes to period-2 oscillation
abstract: This study presents the first numerical evidence of multi-bifurcation routes to period-2 oscillations within an open-loop control framework in a single-element liquid rocket engine burning hydrogen peroxide and methane. To achieve this, a full-scale three-dimensional compressible Detached Eddy Simulation, combined with the PaSR combustion model accounting for coupling between turbulence and finite rate chemical reaction, was employed. We focus on the nonlinear dynamics of thermoacoustic instability and its open-loop control, which involve the coexistence and interaction of oscillations at multiple frequencies within the combustion chamber. The results show that, in the absence of external disturbances, the system spontaneously enters a limit cycle state with constant amplitude and frequency oscillations at the first-order longitudinal (1 L) acoustic frequency (≈1566 Hz). Subsequently, the external sinusoidal disturbances of inlet mass flow rate, with a fixed frequency of 3000 Hz and amplitudes from 10 % to 60 %, lead the system through a series of bifurcations: quasi-periodic (A = 10 %)→chaotic (A = 20 %)→quasi-periodic (A = 40 %)→period-2 (A = 60 %) oscillations. Additionally, we investigate the synchronization between acoustic pressure and flame dynamics under different states, providing insights into the physical mechanisms driving these bifurcations and offering guidance for active control strategies for thermoacoustic instability in liquid rocket engines.

title: Data-driven neurocomputational analysis of couple-stress bioconvective nanofluid transport with Arrhenius activation over a magnetically actuated Riga surface
abstract: The present study develops a computational framework for the analysis of multi-physical transport phenomena, thermal characteristics and bioconvection dynamics of a conducting fluid in contact with an elongating stretching surface coupled with a Riga plate electromagnetic actuator. The transport model also explains the localized MHD control effect through the Lorentz force, which is parallel to the wall and described by the exponential Grinberg term, while also taking into account the stable bioconvection field, which is affected by the microscopic floating of the motile microbes. In order to address the natural convergence and stability, the Parametric Continuation Method (PCM) is used to generate the dataset. The dataset is further solved through the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) based on the Levenberg-Marquardt backpropagation algorithm (LMBPO). The network is trained using the baseline dataset and is able to model the complex cross coupling behavior over a wide parametric range, including changes in the Hartmann and bioconvection Péclet numbers. The surrogate framework provides excellent predictive accuracy by having mean squared errors (MSE) close to zero and a correlation coefficient ( R ) close to on1. Ultimate validation shows that the ANN-LMBPO approach is capable of justifying the numerical instabilities that are typically seen in PCM during aggressive parametric sweep and is also able to instantaneously evaluate the critical engineering quantities like the skin friction coefficient, local Nusselt number and motile microbe’s density number. The energy transfer rate enhances up to 34.6496%, and 44.0358% by varying the mixed convection parameter from 0.5 to 1.5, and heat radiation factor from 0.1 to 0.5, whereas it drops up to 47.5205% with the effect of thermophoresis factor. The mass propagation increases up to 38.196%, 13.1664% and 19.1389% with the variation in mixed convection parameter from 0.5 to 1.5, thermal radiation from 0.1 to 0.5 and thermophoresis from 0.2 to 0.6, respectively.

title: 2.04: Thermal Actuation
abstract: Thermal actuation, as one of the main actuation mechanisms, plays an important role in establishing functional micro-nano-systems. In this chapter, the basic theory of thermal actuation and several widely used thermal actuators are elaborated, including their operational principle and performance. Some potential strategies are discussed for optimization and thus enhancement of their performance. In addition, some major applications of thermal actuators in different fields such as micro-optics, bio-photonics, biomedical chips, microfluidics, wireless communication, nano instrumentation, nanomaterial characterization, soft robotics, and compliant mechanisms are summarized, followed by the discussions of the future trend of thermal actuation.

title: Bridging sensation and actuation: From fundamental architectures to adaptive systems
abstract: Adaptive systems, with their capacity to interact with dynamic environment with self-regulating actions, are driving the development of smart systems across applications ranging from biomedicine and energy to human–machine interfaces. Achieving adaptability requires functional integration between sensors and actuators to transfer from single, fixed operational modes to adaptive behaviors for dynamic scenarios. In this perspective, this review highlights the fundamental mechanisms of tactile sensors and actuators, along with strategies for their functional and performance-level integration. We summarize how adaptive features are embodied in diverse device architectures, revealing distinct characteristics tailored for dynamic functionality at the material and device levels. Furthermore, we focus on application-specific performance enabled by autonomous sensing, regulation, and decision-making. Ultimately, this review outlines key limitations, such as mechanical robustness, dimensional scalability and power management, that need to be overcome to advance adaptive devices from laboratory prototypes to practical, real-world technologies.

title: Bifurcation behavior of hunting motion in high-speed rail vehicles under modal coupling
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical study of hunting bifurcation behavior in high-speed rail vehicles under modal coupling and compares it to the traditional uncoupled system. A dynamic simplified model that integrates the lateral and yaw motions of the rigid bogie and the lateral motion of the carbody is established to evaluate the modal coupled effect between the carbody and bogie. The stability and Hopf bifurcation of the trivial equilibrium are first analyzed qualitatively using the normal form theory. The linear stability analysis then reveals that modal coupling introduces a new unstable region known as carbody (primary) hunting, which is absent in the uncoupled system that only exhibits bogie (secondary) hunting. The double-parameter Hopf bifurcation analysis is further carried out, which considers the influence of suspension parameters on the bifurcation speed and stability region. Our findings indicate that the dynamical behavior of the coupled system can closely match that of the uncoupled system with suitable parameter configurations, effectively reducing primary hunting and enhancing the overall hunting stability of rail vehicles.

title: Predicting freeplay-induced aeroelastic limit-cycle oscillations using pre-critical output data
abstract: This paper presents an output-based approach for predicting aeroelastic limit-cycle oscillations caused by freeplay, a common concentrated stiffness nonlinearity in actuated structures. The approach extends conventional output-based flutter boundary estimation by capturing freeplay-induced nonlinear effects, enabling the prediction of limit-cycle oscillations beyond the flutter onset. It also extends bifurcation forecasting through a new formulation that captures how freeplay nonlinearity affects the recovery rate to equilibrium. The approach is demonstrated using data from simulated time histories of an idealized tilting propeller in airplane mode, with freeplay in the tilting mechanism. Using as few as one or two pre-critical responses, the method estimates regions of the parameter-amplitude plane associated with limit-cycle oscillations, which define the bifurcation diagram. These results indicate promise for the analysis of freeplay-induced limit-cycle oscillations in higher-complexity models and for potential experimental studies.

title: Resilient sampled-data control for fractional-order PMVG-based WTS with actuator saturation and probabilistic faults using fuzzy Lyapunov function method
abstract: The goal of this study is to present a new fuzzy Lyapunov function-based resilient sampled-data control method for a fractional-order permanent magnet vernier generator (PMVG)-based wind turbine system (WTS) that addresses actuator saturation and probabilistic faults. To achieve this, we first model the dynamical fractional model of the PMVG-based WTS as a T-S fuzzy model. Next, we introduce a fuzzy Lyapunov function within a unified framework that incorporates actuator saturation, probabilistic faults, and uncertainty information from control gain matrices. We then present an actuator fault model that represents actuator faults as stochastic variables with a specific probability distribution. Subsequently, we formulate a robust asymptotic stability criterion for closed-loop systems using linear matrix inequality (LMI), which integrates the fuzzy Lyapunov function and membership function information with fractional integral inequality techniques based on sampling time. We also propose an LMI approach to identify the domain of attraction that meets the necessary actuator saturation criteria. Finally, we apply the proposed method to a PMVG-based WTS, demonstrating its superiority and practical applicability through a comparison with existing methods using a numerical example of a nonlinear truck trailer system.

title: Design of a SMA actuated freeplay elimination device for stiffness enhancement of a folding fin
abstract: The folding fin, essential for controlling aircraft flight attitude and maintaining stability, is extensively employed in aerospace vehicles. Inevitable freeplay within the structure, due to design, installation, and mechanical wear, reduce the stiffness of the folding fins and impair the aircraft's aerodynamic performance. Therefore, eliminating the freeplay in the folding fin is crucial for enhancing the aircraft's flight accuracy and stability. This paper introduces a novel freeplay elimination device utilizing SMA columns, which neither increases mass nor alters the aircraft's external dimensions. The device effectively alleviates nonlinear issues associated with gaps in the fin system and enhances both the dynamic and static stiffness of the folding fin. A parametric design model for the gap elimination device has been developed, delineating the relationship between the structure and layout of the SMA columns, the actuation temperature, load, and the target gap for elimination. We conducted static load tests along with modal tests at room and elevated temperatures to evaluate the stiffness enhancement performance of the folding fin before and after gap elimination. The experiments verified that the designed gap elimination device significantly enhances both the static and dynamic stiffness of the folding fin. Additionally, the first-order frequency of the folding fin increased by 40 % at room temperature and by 36.7 % at 200 °C. This paper provides quantifiable guidance for the structural and parametric design of gap elimination devices in folding fins. Optimal structural parameters, determined based on aerodynamic loads and gap elimination requirements, enhance the stiffness of the folding fin, thus improving the aircraft's flight performance.

title: Rub-induced nonlinear vibration and discontinuity-induced bifurcation analysis of a noisy rotor-stator system with different compliant contact force models
abstract: The rotor-stator rubs that may occur due to optimized clearance combined with high shaft vibration are significant issues for machine stability, reliability, and lateral shaft motion. The present work numerically and experimentally investigates the rub-induced nonlinear vibration characteristics and discontinuity-induced bifurcation in a non-smooth Jeffcott rotor-stator system with different forms of compliant rub-impact models subjected to combined unbalance force and noise. First, a two degree-of-freedom (DOF) Jeffcott model with symmetric and asymmetric support stiffness with cross-coupling is considered. Various models for compliant contact have been considered, including Hertz, Kelvin-Voigt, elastic, piecewise linear, and nonlinear dissipative contact force models. Next, a four DOF rotor-stator model is developed, where the rotor impacts the visco-elastically suspended elastic stator model through a nonlinear compliant contact model that includes local stiffness of the stator coating with an elastic wear layer. The effects of unbalance force, friction coefficient, damping coefficient, bearing clearance, shaft nonlinearities, system anisotropy, such as due to gravitational forces, cross-coupling stiffness, asymmetric stiffness, and parametric as well as additive noise on the dynamic response and stability are investigated. The uncertainty is modelled by generating appropriate Gaussian as well as non-Gaussian coloured noise processes, by filtering Gaussian white noise through a first-order linear and nonlinear filter, respectively. The dynamic behaviour is presented using time waveform, whirling motion, Poincare’ section, bifurcation diagram, wavelet transform, recurrence plots and the largest Lyapunov exponent. An experimental study is carried out using a Jeffcott rotor and a movable elastic rod to simulate the rubbing phenomenon. Numerical results are also compared with actual rubbing, as observed during troubleshooting and condition monitoring for various rotating machinery.

title: Bifurcation and stability analysis by tracking energy trajectory of a bolted rotor-bearing system under multi-nonlinearity coupled effect
abstract: The rotor system is a core component of various critical machinery. When nonlinear factors such as nonlinear contact stiffness, oil-film forces, and rub-impact forces are taken into account, the rotor system exhibits considerably complex bifurcation phenomena, complicating its dynamic characteristics and stability conditions. Traditional research methods for rotor systems also have limitations in real-time monitoring of bifurcation phenomena. This paper investigates the bifurcation phenomena and stability issues of the rotor system from an energy perspective. A dynamic equation for the rotor system that considers nonlinear contact stiffness, oil-film forces, and rub-impact forces is established. The steady-state response of the rotor system is obtained using numerical analysis methods, and the relationship between bifurcation and energy transfer is analyzed. Based on theoretical analysis and experimental results, the relationships between three-dimensional energy trajectories, two-dimensional energy trajectories, and the bifurcation forms and stability of the rotor are studied. Experimental tests are conducted on a rotor test bench. The collected data is analyzed to validate the practical effectiveness and applicability of the proposed energy trajectory method in identifying actual bifurcation types in a physical system. The results demonstrate that the energy curve exhibits more detailed fluctuations compared to the smooth displacement curve during the speed-up process, confirming its capability in capturing transient dynamic behaviors. The research indicates that, compared to traditional methods, monitoring the energy transfer in the rotor system can accurately determine its bifurcation phenomena and unstable motions. These findings can be applied to condition monitoring and stability prediction of rotor systems, marking significant progress in the translation of rotor system theory into engineering applications.

title: Vibration energy analysis of rub-impact rotor system: Nonlinear fault-induced energy response and transfer state
abstract: The nonlinear dynamic behavior induced by rub-impact faults constitutes a critical factor that constrains the safe and stable operation of rotor systems. Existing research primarily focuses on analyzing the characteristics of nonlinear responses, but rarely addresses the specific influence of such nonlinear behavior on the system performance. In this paper, the vibration energy method was introduced to investigate the nonlinear response caused by rub-impact of rotor system. The energy characteristics corresponding to different fault states were achieved, and the energy variation law induced by nonlinear bifurcation was elucidated. In addition, the energy transfer ratio was defined to quantify the system's utilization ability of input energy, and the influence of key rub-impact parameters on vibration energy was analyzed. The results demonstrated that the rub-impact fault results in the dissipation of input energy while simultaneously enhancing the energy utilization efficiency of the system. Particularly, when fault induce instability in periodic motion, the energy utilization ability increases sharply, potentially threatening structural safety. Finally, the validity of the proposed method and theoretical analysis was experimentally confirmed. The results provide a theoretical foundation for understanding the mechanisms by which nonlinear responses affect rotor systems and for optimizing structural design.

title: Methodology and conditions for a non-smooth induced bifurcation in a four-degree-of-freedom rotor–stator rubbing system with viscous friction
abstract: In this paper a four-degree-of-freedom piecewise smooth nonlinear rotor–stator rubbing system with viscous friction is systematically investigated. The focus is on developing methodology and unveiling the influence of system parameters on a non-smooth bifurcation in the Filippov system, specifically induced due to the introduction of the viscous friction model. In this system a quasi-periodic partial rub motion is induced just after the rotor comes into contact with the stator from a periodic no-rub motion. This bifurcation is quite different from the Hopf-like bifurcation in the piecewise smooth continuous system since there is solely the bifurcated solution as the only admissible (visible) solution after the bifurcation. The proposed methodology consists of transforming the system into the one in the rotating coordinates so as to transfer the problem into a non-smooth bifurcation from a fixed point to a limit cycle. After presenting the existence conditions for boundary equilibria, a piecewise-linear normal form is constructed through local linearization around them in the neighborhood of the switching manifold. The existence of a pseudo-focus around the switching manifold is then proven, and the presence of stable crossing limit cycles, corresponding to the quasi-periodic partial rub motion of original system, is then confirmed by the Poincaré return map. The proposed approximate model can also well predict the maximum amplitude of quasi-periodic responses. Furthermore, with the developed methodology in hand, the influence of the system parameters on the boundaries separating the region solely with the quasi-periodic partial rub motion and that with coexistence of it and the synchronous full annular rub motion are explored by considering the effect of the viscous damping coefficient of friction.

title: Dynamical characteristics of chattering and grazing bifurcation in a fractional-order coupled impact system
abstract: Impact vibration systems are widely employed in high-end equipment fields such as aerospace and precision manufacturing, whose nonlinear dynamic behaviors directly determine the service performance of the equipment. Complex critical behaviors such as chattering and grazing may lead to component wear, structural failure and precision loss, and can also result in dynamic instability of the system and even induce safety accidents, seriously affecting the operational stability and safety of equipment. Therefore, their prevention and control constitute a key issue urgently to be addressed in engineering. In this paper, a dynamic model of a two-degree-of-freedom impact vibration system with piecewise stiffness, fractional-order damping and strong nonlinear stiffness is firstly established. Subsequently, the chattering characteristics are deduced under three impact conditions, with quantitative analysis of the chattering completion point and evolution duration. Combined with numerical simulation, the regulation mechanisms of chattering modes are clarified. Then, the existence conditions and determination methods for grazing phenomena are derived. Through bidirectional frequency sweep simulation, the hysteresis characteristics, bistable features and periodic motion evolution of grazing bifurcations are revealed. Furthermore, the response distribution characteristics under multi-parameter coupling are explored. Combined with parameter sensitivity analysis, the core control parameters are identified, and a targeted multi-dimensional parameter coordination strategy is proposed. This study elucidates the evolution mechanisms of chattering and grazing bifurcations in impact vibration systems as well as the key control parameters, thereby providing significant practical guidance for the design optimization, safe operation and maintenance of related engineering systems.

title: Establishment of nonlinear dynamic model and study on bifurcation characteristics of non-orthogonal misaligned face gear power split -flow transmission system
abstract: Study on the effects of backlash, friction, and rotational speed on the nonlinear bifurcation characteristics of Non-Orthogonal Misaligned Face Gear Power Split-Flow Transmission System (NOMFGPSFTS), aiming to provide theoretical basis and technical guidance for improving power to weight ratio, prolonging service life, and ensuring the reliability of the power transmission mechanism of innovative helicopters, ships and automobiles. An 11 degree of freedom (DOF), bending, torsion and axis coupling nonlinear dynamic model is established by using the lumped mass method. The model uses Load Tooth Contact Analysis(LTCA) method to calculate the meshing stiffness of Non-Orthogonal Misaligned Face Gear (NOMFG), and combines the key nonlinear elements, including gear tooth surface friction, backlash, support stiffness and transmission error, to facilitate an accurate representation of the system dynamics. The system's dynamic differential equations are solved using the Runge-Kutta algorithm, and the system's nonlinear characteristics are demonstrated through time domain diagrams, Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) spectrograms, phase plane diagrams, Poincaré maps and Maximum Lyapunov Exponent diagrams. Bifurcation diagrams are used to further reveal the effects of backlash, rotational speed, and friction coefficient on the system's nonlinear behavior. The study finds that with the increase of dimensionless backlash, the system transits from periodic-1 motion to chaotic motion, and may evolve into periodic-2 motion, showing obvious nonlinear vibrations. With the increase of rotating speed, the system transits from periodic-2 motion to chaotic motion, and finally realizes periodic-1 motion. With the increase of friction coefficient, the chaotic region of the system decreases. Finally, the correctness of the theoretical model is verified by experiments, which provides a theoretical basis for the stability study of the system.

title: Semi-analytical predictions of multi-stable independent periodic motions and bifurcation evolution in a nonlinear bolted rotor system
venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation
abstract: The bolted structures have the advantages of high specific strength and easy maintenance, which are widely used in rotating machines such as gas turbines and aero-engines. Meanwhile, the complex nonlinear motions and bifurcations are easily induced by the nonlinear stiffness caused by the bolted structure in rotor systems, but these characteristics cannot be fully revealed only by numerical results. In this research, an analytical model of a bolted rotor system considering contact nonlinearity is established. The global bifurcation trees and semi-analytical periodic motions of the system are presented by the implicit discrete mapping method, which are also compared to the numerical solutions for validation. Multi-stable phenomena of independent periodic motions P-3(m+1), (m = 0, 1, 2) are discovered, the bifurcation jumping phenomena between the higher-order and lower-order motions are revealed, the occurrence of unstable motions is indicated in Neimark bifurcation judged by eigenvalues. In addition, the independence of the higher-order periodic motions in bifurcation tree is proved. Finally, the periodic motions of the nonlinear rotor system are numerically predicted by harmonic amplitudes and phase characteristics. These findings provide clear and complete solutions for understanding and presenting the nonlinear dynamic characteristics of bolted rotor systems considering the contact effect, which have great potential in guiding the dynamic design and parameter adjustment of practical rotating machines.

title: Bifurcation analysis of a self-excited oscillator with quasi-zero-stiffness properties
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical study of both conventional and non-smooth bifurcations in a friction-driven self-excited oscillator. A distinctive feature of the model is its Van der Pol damping and nonlinear restoring force, which includes a cubic term and is designed to function as an equivalent quasi-zero-stiffness device. Firstly, theoretical conditions for the occurrence of various sliding bifurcations are established. Secondly, when equilibrium points are located in some region, their stability conditions and the existence criteria for both supercritical and subcritical Hopf bifurcations are derived. It is well known that there is little theoretical research on bifurcations in non-smooth systems and these research findings bridge the theoretical gaps in the analysis of non-smooth dynamical systems. The theoretical analysis is validated through numerical simulations, which confirms the presence of sliding bifurcations (crossing–sliding bifurcation, grazing–sliding bifurcation, switching–sliding bifurcation), as well as supercritical and subcritical Hopf bifurcations. Furthermore, we observe that a periodic orbit emerging from a supercritical Hopf bifurcation, upon further parameter variation, may begin to intersect the switching boundary, leading to various sliding bifurcations, which is different from the phenomenon described in previous references. A novel coexistence of subcritical Hopf bifurcation and crossing–sliding bifurcation, or switching–sliding bifurcation is found, which is rarely reported in prior studies. In a word, this study provides a refined theoretical framework for analyzing both sliding bifurcations and Hopf bifurcations in non-smooth dynamical systems.

title: Rich nonlinear dynamic behaviors in a two-parameter plane for the rubbing rotor system
abstract: The development of rubbing faults and the associated dynamic responses in a rotor system is cumulative and progressive. One-parameter mapping cannot fully reveal the system's potential dynamic behavior, which may be unstable and could lead to system failure. To effectively reveal these potential dynamic characteristics, this study presents a method of dynamic mapping in a two-parameter plane based on the idea of gridding. The formation mechanisms of various dynamic responses of the rubbing rotor system were studied in the parameter space and state space. The rubbing state of the rotor can be effectively characterized by the proposed method for calculating the dynamic rubbing rate (DRR) of the rotor. The results demonstrated that the two-parameter plane can enrich and precisely describe the dynamic behavior and multi-state coexistence of the rotor system, such as periodic motion or chaos, and multiple bifurcation features. This study investigated the relationship between the periodic motion of the rotational system and two key parameters: rotor-stator clearance and rotational speed. Reducing the clearance increases response complexity and can trigger both full annular rub and full non-annular rub. Increasing stator stiffness enhances the system's sub-harmonic frequency response, leading to instability, multi-period motion and chaos. Multiple bifurcation patterns are observed across various initial-value domains. Periodic Saddle-node bifurcations induce significant changes in rotor amplitude and DRR, also causing coexistence of multiple states and generating fractal basins of attraction. In contrast, other bifurcations result in erosion of the attraction domain. To validate these findings, experiments were conducted on a rub-impact rotor test bench. By analyzing the system in both parameter and state spaces, this study reveals the rich dynamic behavior of the rotor system, providing valuable insights for the identification of rubbing faults and the prediction of system dynamics.

title: Bifurcation criterion of faults in complex nonlinear systems
abstract: In this paper, we introduce bifurcation theory into complex nonlinear systems. We adopt a novel approach to identify faults in electric circuit systems. After accidents occur without warning, with large numbers of complicated and high-precision calculations, we use bifurcation results of corresponding amplitude and frequency (period) to analyze their universal characteristics. Based on super attractive parameters, we have got the universal constant 4.6692.... The results from the present investigation imply that each fault in an electric circuit system must correspond to one or more bifurcation locations, which will provide a bifurcation criterion of faults in complex nonlinear systems. This research will have a significant theoretical value and engineering practical significance. © 2014 Elsevier B.V.

title: Bifurcation and coexistence characteristics of cross stiffness-rubbing rotor system in parameter-state space
venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation
abstract: The variation of cross-stiffness at rotor support locations induces diverse dynamic responses in the system, while complex interactions among system parameters hinder the revelation of underlying dynamics. Therefore, the present study proposes a global method for computing dynamic bifurcations in the ( u,v )-two-dimensional parameter plane (TDPP) based on a regional discretization approach. This method incorporates a multi-state composite Poincaré section. Furthermore, a dynamic stability rate is introduced to quantify the severity of instability in rubbing rotors. By applying this global approach, the existence regions and bifurcation behaviors of various attractors in the TDPP of the cross-stiffness rubbing (CSR) rotor system are calculated and identified. The results show that the TDPP can enrich and precisely describe the dynamic behavior and multi-state coexistence of the rotor system, such as periodic motion or chaos, along with multiple bifurcation features. The system response is highly sensitive to cross stiffness, and an increase in cross stiffness exacerbates system rubbing and instability. When the cross stiffness exceeds the threshold, the vibration reduction effect achieved by increasing clearance or damping is significantly weakened. Additionally, periodic saddle-node bifurcation under multi-initial value conditions alters the topological structure of the response, which is the fundamental cause of the coexistence of multiple attractors and the fractal of the basin of attraction. These findings provide valuable insights for improving the design and dynamic control of rotor systems.

title: Nonlinear vibration behavior of a hinged-hinged flexible beam with fractional damping and DTD feedback control
abstract: With analytical and numerical methods, this paper investigates the complex nonlinear dynamics of a harmonically excited hinged-hinged flexible beam integrated with distributed time-delay (DTD) feedback control and fractional damping. The governing equation is modeled as a generalized fractional-order Duffing-van der Pol (DVP) oscillator under combined parametric and forced excitations and reduced to an effective integer-order slow system. Through perturbation analysis, the unperturbed system's Hamiltonian structure is classified into single-well (SW), double-well (DW), and triple-well (TW) potential configurations, with stability and static bifurcation conditions rigorously established. Explicit analytical expressions for homoclinic, heteroclinic, and periodic orbits within the TW configuration are derived. The Melnikov method is employed to obtain analytical criteria for the onset of Smale horseshoe chaos. The subharmonic bifurcation conditions induced by different periodic intersections are rigorously derived by subharmonic Melnikov method. The results demonstrate that the chaotic threshold and bifurcation pathways of this system can be effectively modulated by the DTD decay rate and the order of the fractional derivative. Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical predictions and reveal two distinct pathways to chaos: via a cascade of even-order subharmonic bifurcations controlled by the parametric excitation amplitude, and via odd-order subharmonic bifurcations controlled by the forcing amplitude.

title: Imbalance-induced nonlinear vibrations in wind turbine towers
abstract: This paper investigates the nonlinear dynamic response of a wind turbine tower under rotor imbalances. A coupled analytical model for a three-bladed horizontal-axis turbine on a tapered monopole tower is developed, using a Lagrangian formulation, with the nonlinear equations of motion derived via Hamilton's principle. The model incorporates a nonlinear aerodynamic torque, enabling accurate dynamic representation under varying conditions. In contrast to prevalent uncoupled models, this novel formulation captures essential nonlinear interactions and energy transfer between the tower and rotor. The equations are solved using an explicit Runge-Kutta method, and a customized continuation scheme analyses system bifurcations, identifying instability via Floquet multipliers. Results demonstrate that even small blade mass imbalances significantly amplify the tower's dynamic response, with effects increasing with imbalance severity. Comparisons with uncoupled models highlight the critical role of nonlinear coupling. These findings support improved design and assessment of wind turbine towers under fault conditions to avoid resonant or damaging behavior.

title: Forced Ueda oscillator: Basin and bifurcation analysis in parameter space
abstract: The degenerate forced harmonic Duffing oscillator with zero linear stiffness, commonly known as the Ueda oscillator has long been known as a canonical benchmark in nonlinear dynamics and chaos theory. The global dynamics of the Ueda oscillator are investigated through behavioural maps in the forcing amplitude–frequency plane. This methodology not only identifies dangerous and safe parameter combinations with respect to the transmitted acceleration amplitude, but also elucidates how the onset of chaotic dynamics can significantly amplify acceleration levels, offering valuable insights into the complex interplay between chaos and vibration transmission in nonlinear dynamical systems. The results reveal several remarkable phenomena in the structure of the behavioural maps, including: (i) the existence of large, compact regions of chaotic dynamics; (ii) the emergence of sparse (meagre) sets of chaos distributed across broad ranges of forcing frequencies and amplitudes; (iii) the formation of chaotic regions resembling Arnold tongues; and (iv) the presence of distinctive dynamical regimes at small frequency range. This analysis highlights how parameter space basin structures can guide the selection of safe operating regimes for highly nonlinear seismic isolation devices, where low acceleration transmission is critical. The analysis is based on solving the equations of motion by the Adams–Bashforth–Moulton (ABM) predictor-corrector method, enabling numerically stable computations over long time intervals.

title: Fractional-order FitzHugh–Nagumo dynamics: From single-neuron stability bifurcations to synchronization in small-world networks
venue: Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications
abstract: This study pioneers a unified theoretical framework for fractional-order (FO) FitzHugh–Nagumo (FHN) neurodynamics, uncovering novel order-dependent and topology-order synergetic regulation mechanisms. By integrating FO stability theory with an extended master stability function approach, we achieve three pivotal breakthroughs: First, we identify a novel order-dependent stability bifurcation in single FOFHN neurons, where a reduced order enhances nodal stability via the intrinsic memory effects of FO calculus. Second, FOFHN networks exhibit counterintuitive non-monotonic synchronization bifurcations, which reveal the dual regulatory role of memory effects: while FO memory effects stabilize individual neurons, they can either facilitate or impair synchronous behavior at the network scale. Third, we discover unique nonlinear interactions between small-world topology and fractional order that generate distinct network synchronization patterns, where optimal synchronization arises from the balanced interplay of fractional order, topological structure, and nodal dynamical properties. This work bridges critical gaps in cross-scale FO neurodynamics, offering fundamental new insights into memory-dependent neuronal dynamics and establishing practical design principles for the modeling and control of FO neuronal networks.

title: Nonlinear dynamic response of non-circular gear planetary trains considering tooth surface flash temperature
venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation
abstract: The 4–6-stage non-circular gear planetary train (NCPG) is a key transmission component in hydraulic motors. To investigate the influence of tooth surface flash temperature on the dynamic characteristics of the NCPG, the flash temperature and thermally induced tooth profile deformation of the internal and external meshing pairs were calculated based on H. Blok's flash temperature theory. The effects of meshing frequency and contact load on flash temperature and deformation were analyzed, and a 36-degree-of-freedom nonlinear dynamic model incorporating flash temperature effects was established. The bifurcation, impact, and dynamic load characteristics of the system under single- and dual-parameter excitations were studied, and the dynamic behaviors with and without flash temperature effects were compared. The results show that the flash temperature and tooth profile deformation reach their maximum when the driving gear root contacts the driven gear tip, and decrease to zero at the pitch point. As the meshing frequency and contact load increase, the flash temperature and deformation intensify, leading to reductions in both the time-varying meshing stiffness and backlash. Variations in excitation frequency lead to rich bifurcation, dynamic load, and impact characteristics in the system. A large error excitation amplitude significantly expands the range of chaotic motion in the low- and medium-frequency regions, deteriorates the impact state, and notably increases the dynamic load. An increase in the meshing damping ratio substantially reduces or even completely eliminates chaotic motion in the system, introduces an impact-free motion interval, and significantly reduces the dynamic load imposed on the system, maintaining it at a relatively low level. The flash temperature introduces more complex bifurcation characteristics, significantly increases the dynamic load, and worsens the impact state. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the dynamic design and vibration control of NCPGs.

title: Accurate nonlinear time-periodic model and stability analysis of LCC-HVDC considering commutation failure and switching control
venue: International Journal of Electrical Power & Energy Systems
abstract: Line-commutated-converter based high-voltage direct current (LCC-HVDC) systems are essential for long-distance bulk power transmission, yet accurately modeling their dynamics under complex operating conditions remains challenging due to non-smoothness, nonlinearity, time-periodicity, and control mode switching. This paper develops a unified smooth nonlinear time-periodic ordinary differential equation (ODE) model for LCC-HVDC by approximating the switching dynamics. The proposed model accommodates both symmetrical conditions (SCs) and asymmetrical conditions (ASCs), as well as abnormal transients caused by commutation failure (CF) and controller switching. On this basis, the small-signal (SS) stability of steady-state periodic orbits (PO) under off-nominal conditions is analyzed using Poincaré map and numerical continuation, and the stability boundaries of controllers under the switching control scheme and external grid are obtained. In addition, a large-signal (LS) stability analysis method based on the Poincaré recurrence theorem is proposed to identify coexisting attractors and quantify stability under large perturbations. Results show that off-nominal operating conditions may trigger Neimark–Sacker and fold bifurcations, while some controller parameters have little effect on SS stability but significantly reduce LS stability The effectiveness of the proposed modeling and analysis framework is verified using both the CIGRE benchmark model and a real-world project in South China.

title: A fast search method for optimal parameters of stochastic resonance based on stochastic bifurcation and its application in fault diagnosis of rolling bearings
abstract: Stochastic resonance (SR) is a fascinating nonlinear phenomenon that uses appropriate external noise to enhance the specified weak signal. Therefore, it has been widely studied in weak signal detection. Because of this, This paper puts forward a model of considering the time-delay stochastic resonance from the perspective of engineering applications, Colored noise as external ambient noise. At the same time, the classical bistable symmetric potential is changed into a double-well variable potential well which can directly control the barrier height through parameters. In addition, this paper finds a more effective search interval by studying the random bifurcation of the system, which can improve the search efficiency by about 50%. Finally, the new model is compared with the Duffing model without time-delay from the experiment and engineering application perspective. The new model increases the amplitude of the target signal more effectively under the condition of restraining low-frequency and high-frequency interference and then verifies the effectiveness and superiority of the method proposed in this paper in engineering practice.

title: Stability assessment considering multi-timescale power system dynamics: Insights into Hopf bifurcations with GFL and GFM IBRs
abstract: Real power systems exhibit dynamics that evolve across a wide range of timescales, from very fast to very slow phenomena. Historically, incorporating these wide-ranging dynamics into a single model has been impractical. As a result, power engineers rely on timescale decomposition to simplify models. When evaluating fast phenomena, slow dynamics are often neglected (assumed constant), and vice versa. This paper underscores the limitations of this traditional approach by demonstrating the importance of assessing power system stability while considering multiple timescales simultaneously. Using the concept of Hopf bifurcations, the study illustrates instability issues that would be missed if multi-timescale dynamics are not considered. Specifically, it exemplifies a class of instability that is overlooked when multi-timescale dynamics are decoupled, with a particular emphasis on networks featuring inverter-based resources.

title: Positive role of bifurcation on stochastic resonance and its application in fault diagnosis under time-varying rotational speed
abstract: Stochastic resonance (SR) is mainly produced by the synergistic effect of noise, nonlinear system, and signals. This converts a part of the noise energy into useful signal energy, thereby improving the output of the system. When rotating machinery starts and stops, driving force and load will cause the variation of speed, and thus the produced vibration signal has strong non-stationary characteristics. Furthermore, although SR can be used to process non-stationary signals, its system parameters need to be matched in real-time, and therefore its application and development are limited. This paper mainly studies an adaptive frequency-shift SR of the tri-stable nonlinear system. On the one hand, order analysis can transform non-stationary signals into stationary signals, which shows the advantages of SR in stationary signal processing. On the other hand, the change of system parameters switches the system from tri-stable state to bistable and monostable state, so it loses the advantage of tri-stable weak signal detection. The variation of potential well depth, bifurcation phenomenon, and steady-state switching process caused by system parameters are studied, to help facilitate the control of the system parameters to determine the steady-state situation. Finally, SR is applied to the fault diagnosis of rolling bearing under variable speed conditions and the background of strong noise, which effectively extracts weak fault features.

title: Modal reduction-based analysis of nonlinear vibrations and chaotic dynamics in beam structures
abstract: Nonlinear beam models play a crucial role in the analysis and design of flexible structural components used in aerospace structures, mechanical systems, and civil engineering applications, where large deformations, geometric nonlinearities, and instability phenomena strongly influence dynamic performance. The considered nonlinear beam system provides an effective framework for examining complex vibration behavior and nonlinear stability characteristics beyond the limits of linear theory. By adopting the Euler–Bernoulli formulation, the continuous beam model is reduced into a single governing ordinary differential equation through modal reduction based on the Galerkin approach. A comprehensive dynamical analysis is conducted using a wide range of chaos detection and characterization tools, including two- and three-dimensional phase portraits, time-series analysis, Poincaré maps, iterative return maps, power spectra, bifurcation diagrams, chaotic attractors, and Lyapunov exponents. The numerical results reveal periodic, quasi-periodic, and chaotic responses under different control parameters. In addition to the numerical investigations, analytical polynomial and rational solutions of the reduced nonlinear equation are derived under the special condition ω1=0. Under this condition, the reduced system exhibits a neutral equilibrium configuration in which static deformation dominates over oscillatory motion. These findings provide useful insights into the stability assessment and controllable design of nonlinear beam-type structures operating under large-deformation conditions.

title: Nonlinear dynamics of planetary gear transmission systems considering gear wear
abstract: Endowed with excellent torque distribution performance, high load-bearing capacity and a compact, space-saving structural design, planetary gear transmissions are extensively utilized in core domains such as automotive gearboxes, engineering machinery, aerospace equipment and precision transmission devices. In the present study, a high-fidelity dynamic model characterizing the planetary gear train is developed by comprehensively incorporating surface wear faults of the gear teeth. Subsequently, the governing nonlinear ordinary differential equations (ODEs) describing the entire system are rigorously derived and constructed in detail. Through numerical computation and solution, a series of insightful simulation results are generated, featuring bifurcation diagrams depicting system evolution, time-domain response waveforms, phase trajectory evolution diagrams, wavelet-based time-frequency characterization plots, Lyapunov exponent evolution analysis plots and dynamic meshing force diagrams. This research systematically elucidates the evolutionary laws of how meshing excitation frequency and gear wear degree exert a significant influence on the nonlinear vibrational characteristics of the transmission mechanism. Finally, comprehensive simulation experiments are conducted to thoroughly verify the engineering applicability and reliability of the constructed dynamic model.

title: Research on nonlinear vibration characteristics of a dual-axis rotary table system under the coupling of workpiece effects
abstract: Five-axis computer numerical control (CNC) machine tools are developing toward turn-milling compound machining and high-speed operations, which imposes higher demands on the dynamic performance of their key component—the dual-axis rotary table. However, few studies have considered the nonlinear vibration of the dual-axis rotary table under the coupling effect of workpiece eccentricity. To address this issue, this paper establishes a seven-degrees-of-freedom nonlinear bearing-rotor dynamic model incorporating the coupling effect of workpiece eccentricity. Considering the unique structural characteristics of the rotary table support bearings (three-row roller bearings), the stiffness characteristics of the bearings under radial and axial loads are derived and calculated separately. The validity of the proposed model is then verified through experiments. Based on this model, the effects of rotational speed, bearing clearance, eccentricity, and eccentric mass on the dynamic response and chaotic bifurcation phenomena of the system are analyzed. The results show that the vibration amplitude of the system is positively correlated with both rotational speed and eccentric mass; larger bearing clearance aggravates chaotic motion, whereas an appropriate negative clearance suppresses chaos, and the eccentricity significantly affects the periodic motion patterns of the system. This study contributes to a deeper understanding of the dynamic mechanisms of dual-axis rotary table systems and provides theoretical foundations for vibration control and stability enhancement of CNC machine tool systems.

title: LLM-based bearing faults diagnosis via structured spectral text from voltages outputs of nonlinear piezoelectric energy harvester
abstract: Nonlinear piezoelectric energy harvesters (PEHs) can convert ambient vibration into electrical energy and produce voltage responses carrying source dynamics, making self-powered fault monitoring possible. However, the voltage responses generated by a nonlinear PEH is a physically reconstructed response shaped by the nonlinearity of the harvesters. Whether such responses are still reliable for bearing fault diagnosis using a language-compatible diagnostic representation remains un-explored. In this study, a self-powered bearing fault diagnosis framework is developed by combining nonlinear PEH modeling, structured spectral textualization, and large language model (LLM)-based classification. Monostable and bistable PEH models are established, and real bearing vibration signals from the Case Western Reserve University dataset are introduced as excitation. Generated voltage responses are converted into structured spectral text in 16 dimensions, and the diagnosis task is then carried out by Qwen3–8B sequence classification model with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning strategy. The results show that the PEH reconstructs the signal through spectral redistribution and nonlinear modulation, and the bistable state provides higher harvested energy but introduces stronger nonlinear distortion. The proposed textual strategy preserves sufficient discriminative information for later LLM-based diagnosis under both states. These experiments indicate that nonlinear PEHs can serve as power supplies as well as information carriers, providing a basis for self-powered monitoring systems.

title: Nonlinear dynamic evolution and extended contact analysis of helical gears under angular misalignment error
venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation
abstract: Angular misalignment error is a pervasive and critical issue in helical gear transmission systems, typically stemming from assembly imperfections and inherent manufacturing deviations. Despite its significance, existing research often fails to comprehensively integrate the extended tooth contact effect into analytical models, leaving the mechanisms of nonlinear dynamic evolution under multi-directional misalignment insufficiently explored. To bridge this gap, this study systematically investigates the contact mechanics and dynamic behavior of helical gears under directional angular misalignment errors. A novel Loaded Tooth Contact Analysis (LTCA) model is formulated, incorporating both angular misalignment and extended contact effects, which is subsequently integrated into a comprehensive six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) nonlinear dynamic model. Our findings elucidate that angular misalignment significantly exacerbates load concentration and induces severe edge contact, leading to a substantial rise in maximum unit load. Notably, the time-varying mesh stiffness (TVMS) exhibits the highest sensitivity to x -direction misalignment, showing a more pronounced degradation compared to other directions. Furthermore, the research identifies the critical thresholds and evolutionary paths of the system’s nonlinear response. As misalignment magnitude increases, the system transitions from stable periodic motion to chaotic oscillation via period-doubling bifurcations. Crucially, comprehensive misalignment is found to trigger these nonlinear transitions at significantly lower error magnitudes compared to single-axis deviations, highlighting the severe impact of multi-directional coupling. The theoretical model is rigorously validated through an experimental test rig, with measured vibration data and Root Mean Square (RMS) trends showing high concordance with simulation results. These insights provide a robust theoretical foundation for the high-precision design and error-source identification of advanced gear transmission systems.

title: Control performance of nonlinear stiffness inerter system under variable frequency and amplitude excitation
abstract: With the development of new materials and new structural systems, the frequency range corresponding to the main modes of complex structures is becoming broader, and the traditional linear vibration control system is difficult to meet the requirements of broadband control. This paper proposes a nonlinear stiffness inerter system (NSIS) to explore the possibility for lightweight and broadband control. Firstly, the constitutive assumptions of NSIS components and system are verified by experiments. Secondly, the influence of NSIS parameter variation on its control performance is investigated for different amplitude and frequency of the external excitation. Finally, by comparing with other classical tuned dampers, the advantages of NSIS under different control objectives such as single-mode control and multi-mode control are verified. The findings indicate that when the linear stiffness and damping of NSIS align with the bifurcation conditions, an optimal nonlinear stiffness value exists that can minimize the response of the main structure under the excitation of the small amplitude resonance region. Also, the control efficacy of NSIS is similar to the inerter-based damping systems in the resonant region under large-amplitude broadband excitation. Nevertheless, NSIS exhibits significantly superior performance in the non-resonant region. Furthermore, with regard to the multi-degree-of-freedom structure, the NSIS is capable of controlling multiple modes simultaneously, whereas other classical tuned damping systems exhibits a superior control effect for a single mode alone.

title: Dynamics of a nonlinear oscillator with space–time phase-modulated excitation
abstract: The dynamics of rotating machinery systems are often described by non-autonomous ordinary differential equations with time-dependent periodic excitation. However, our recent investigation has revealed that the time-dependent periodic excitation becomes state-dependent through a phase-modulation mechanism when considering torsional dynamics. This phenomenon is observed in various scenarios, such as drilling anisotropic rocks in oil and gas exploration, turning on a lathe with an unbalanced workpiece, and rub-impact rotors with torsional vibrations. The state-dependent nature of the external excitation introduces a novel type of nonlinearity that has not been extensively studied. Similar to the cubic stiffness in Duffing systems and the nonlinear damping in the van der Pol oscillator, the proposed state-dependent excitation can lead to quantitative and qualitative changes in system dynamics. To focus on the core of this nonlinearity, we consider the general form of the proposed nonlinear system as ẍ+γẋ+αx+βsin(ωt+κx)=0. Here, α, β, γ, ω, and κ are parameters, while x and t are the state variable and time, respectively. The excitation term depends on both the state variable x and time t, leading us to name this nonlinear mechanism “space–time phase modulation” in our research. Focusing on this simple oscillator with space–time phase-modulated excitation, bifurcation diagrams of the limit cycles reveal saddle–node bifurcations, period-doubling, super-harmonic resonances, and sub-harmonic resonances in the system. An experimentally observed heart-shaped period-2 attractor in a servo motor with feedback control shows qualitative agreement with the numerical simulations. Further investigation indicates that complex nonlinear behavior, such as quasi-periodic and chaotic motion, emerges as the magnitude of β increases. Ultimately, the proposed space–time phase modulation mechanism provides a new perspective for a better understanding of complex nonlinear dynamics in engineering applications.

title: Bifurcation and stability analysis of a nonlinear rotor system subjected to constant excitation and rub-impact
abstract: This paper focuses on the mechanism of a complex bifurcation behavior caused by flight maneuvers in an aircraft rub-impact rotor system with Duffing type nonlinearity. The maneuver load during flight maneuvers may induce a rub-impact phenomenon, accompanied by complex nonlinear behaviors such as periodic, sub-harmonic and quasi-periodic motions, but the bifurcation mechanism is not so clear. In this study, the harmonic balance method combined with an alternating frequency/time domain procedure (HB-AFT method) is formulated and used to derive the approximate periodic solutions of the system. In conjunction with the arc-length continuation, the solution branches for both periodic 1-T motion (synchronous oscillation) and periodic 2-T motion (sub-harmonic oscillation) are traced. Then with the aid of the Floquet theory, the stabilities of the obtained periodic solutions are examined. The changes in the number or the stability of the solutions lead to the identification of the bifurcation points, which can be classified qualitatively into three types, i.e. Neimark-Sacker bifurcation point (NSBP), quasi-periodic Hopf bifurcation point (QPHBP) and saddle-node bifurcation point (SNBP). In addition, the constant excitation significantly affects the instability as well as the bifurcation of the rotor system. In the case of a smaller constant excitation, the rotation region with respect to the quasi-periodic motions may disappear, accompanied with a PBP (pitchfork bifurcation point) instead of the two NSBPs and one QPHBP. The bifurcation analysis in this paper provides deep insight into the mechanism of the complex nonlinear phenomenon induced by the constant excitation. The results obtained will also contribute to a better understanding of the nonlinear dynamic behaviors of aircraft rotor systems during flight maneuvers.

title: Nonlinear dynamics of a misaligned and eccentric rotor system with three base motions
abstract: Misalignment and eccentricity are common major faults in rotor systems, which significantly affect vibration characteristics of rotor systems. This study aims to investigate dynamic responses of a coupling-misaligned and eccentric rotor system supported by four ball bearings with cubic nonlinear contact stiffness under three base motions, i.e., base rolling, pitching, and hovering motions, contributing to a deeper understanding of vibration characteristics of rotor dynamic systems in space transportation equipment. Equations of motion of the rotor system under base motions are derived by using the Lagrangian method. The incremental harmonic balance method is used to obtain periodic solutions of the rotor system under base motions, and the Floquet theory along with the precise Hsu's method is employed to analyze stability of periodic solutions and their bifurcations. It is found that vibration intensity of the rotor system is not always aggravated under the effect of a base motion load, and it can even be suppressed in some conditions. Nevertheless, response characteristics at even multiples of the shaft rotation frequency for the misalignment fault remain significant, and these fault characteristics are consistent with those observed when the base is fixed. In addition, base motions affect the amplitude of the constant vibration response in frequency domain, leading to the deviation of disk center trajectories. Disk center trajectories shift direction varies with base motion types, potentially causing rotor-stator rubbing impacts at different locations. Furthermore, it is found that nonlinear behaviors of the rotor system change with base motions, including differences in bifurcation types and rotation speeds corresponding to bifurcations. These findings provide theoretical support for the structural design and fault diagnosis of transportation equipment that frequently undergoes spatial motions, such as aircraft engines.

title: A clamped-clamped electromagnetic energy harvester exploiting geometric nonlinearity for helicopter tail shafts
abstract: Due to the lack of external installation space, energy harvesters for condition monitoring need to be embedded inside the hollow helicopter tail shaft. However, the absence of a stationary reference frame renders traditional separated schemes infeasible, while extreme centrifugal loads make conventional self-contained designs (e.g., cantilever beam or in-pipe sliding oscillator) highly susceptible to structural failure or friction jamming. Consequently, this paper proposes an embedded electromagnetic energy harvester based on a clamped-clamped beam architecture, using large-deformation geometric nonlinearity to reduce structural failure risk. A nonlinear electromechanical coupling model under composite motion conditions is established using the Euler-Bernoulli beam theory and Lagrange equations. The analysis demonstrates that rotational motion modulates gravity into periodic excitation. The competition between geometric nonlinear stiffness and centrifugal softening induces a pronounced hardening effect that significantly broadens the response bandwidth within the operating range.
