These competing effects lead to a dynamic bifurcation into a bistable regime at higher rotational velocities. Within the effective rotational speed range of 1000 to 2300 rpm, the prototype achieves a maximum load power of 108 mW. At 2024 rpm, the harvested energy supported a fully integrated real-time wireless vibration sensing node with a stable transmission distance exceeding 10 m, providing a promising technical solution for battery-free monitoring of helicopters.

title: Three-dimensional nonlinear dynamics of pipes conveying pulsatile fluid subjected to external cross flow
abstract: This paper investigates the three-dimensional nonlinear dynamics of pipes conveying pulsatile fluid simultaneously subjected to external cross flow. The governing equations are derived using Hamilton's principle, discretized via the Galerkin's method, and numerically solved by the Runge-Kutta integration algorithm. First, frequency and stability analyses are performed to examine the variations of the three lowest natural frequencies with internal flow velocity and to identify parametric instability regions by means of Floquet theory. Subsequently, bifurcation characteristics are systematically analyzed with the internal pulsating frequency and the external flow velocity as key parameters. The results reveal that the hybrid excitations can induce rich and complex parametric resonance phenomena, including pronounced combination, subharmonic, and superharmonic resonances, demonstrating the system's strong nonlinearity. A particularly noteworthy finding is the synergistic resonance between internal and external flows, which occurs when the internal pulsating frequency approaches certain integer multiples of the external vortex-shedding frequency, resulting in intensified pipe resonance. These findings provide new insights into the nonlinear resonance mechanisms of fluid-conveying pipes under multi-source fluid excitations and offer valuable guidance for engineering design and vibration suppression.

title: Construction of a new Lorenz-like system with cubic nonlinearity and its application in weak signal detection
abstract: To investigate the application value of the Lorenz system in weak signal detection for rolling bearing vibrations, this study innovatively proposes an improved Lorenz system model incorporating a cubic nonlinear term. This improvement not only enhances the system's performance in weak signal detection but also provides new research perspectives for a deeper understanding of nonlinear dynamic behaviors. The study focuses on analyzing the influence mechanism of the cubic nonlinear term on the system's chaotic characteristics and systematically examines the practical application effectiveness of this improved model in weak signal detection. Under constant parameter conditions, a systematic sensitivity analysis was conducted to evaluate the dynamical implications of introducing cubic nonlinearities into the first two governing equations of the system. Our research reveals that as one of the control parameters decreases, the system exhibits a singular degenerate heteroclinic cycles structure, whose collapse process establishes a crucial evolutionary pathway toward chaotic states. In the end, by utilizing the transient chaotic characteristics of the novel Lorenz-like system with cubic terms, we propose a method capable of detecting weak signals in strong noise environments and performing mechanical fault diagnosis. Its effectiveness has been verified through both simulations and experimental validation.

title: Nonlinear vibration of a shaft-disk-shaft rotor with initial bending induced by bearing angular misalignment
abstract: The bolted flange spigot connected rotor plays a critical role in rotating machinery due to its high reliability and load-carrying capacity. Nevertheless, bearing angular misalignment, one of the common assembly errors, not only changes the internal contact state of the bearing but also induces initial bending of the rotor, posing a significant challenge to the dynamic performance of the rotor. Existing research lacks investigations into initial bending faults in rotors connected by bolted flanges with spigot joints. In this study, using Euler-Bernoulli beam theory for the shafts and Kirchhoff plate theory for the disk, the nonlinear dynamic model of a bolted flange spigot-connected shaft-disk-shaft rotor (BFSSDSR) is established, accounting for the initial bending resulting from bearing angular misalignment. Based on the model, the effects of rotational speed, misalignment angle, and the phase difference on the rotor’s vibration characteristics are investigated. The results show that the BFSSDSR with initial bending exhibits multiple harmonic responses as well as combination frequency responses associated with the bearing variable compliance frequency. With the variation of rotational speed, the motion state of the rotor system alternates between periodic motion and chaotic/quasi-periodic motion. An increase in the misalignment angle significantly enhances the synchronous vibration response induced by the initial bending, causing the system spectrum to gradually concentrate around the rotational frequency. Moreover, the phase difference between the initial bending and unbalance mainly modulates the spatial distribution of the synchronous response, significantly affecting the rotor orbit shape without altering the frequency components of the system.

title: Nonlinear dynamic characteristics of flexible bolted rotor system supported by journal bearings considering time varying bending stiffness of flange interface
abstract: Rotating machinery is typically constructed by connecting components made of different materials using bolted joints. In this paper, the time varying bending stiffness, surface morphology, and unbalanced preload are incorporated into the modeling of a bolted flexible rotor system supported by journal bearings. To improve the numerical stability and accuracy of the proposed nonlinear dynamic model, a Newmark-based method incorporating both energy dissipation and disturbance compensation is developed to solve the nonlinear dynamic equation. The proposed model of the bolted rotor system and the Newmark-based method are verified by the experiment. The nonlinear dynamic behaviors and bifurcation characteristics of the bolted rotor system under different rotational speeds are investigated using orbit diagrams, Poincaré maps, bifurcation diagrams, and frequency spectrum diagrams. Finally, the influence of the bolted preload on the dynamic behaviors of the bolted rotor system is also studied. Compared with the integral rotor system, the bolted-joint rotor system exhibits period-doubling bifurcation at a lower rotational speed, and the operational speed range for this bifurcation widens. Elevating the bolt preload delays the period-doubling bifurcation onset speed, widens the operational range of period-doubling motion, and consequently increases the transition speed to quasi-periodic or chaotic regimes.

title: Effects of contact stiffness on the nonlinear motions induced by impacts on an overhung rotor system
venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation
abstract: The effects of contact stiffness between the rotor and stator on the internal resonance of forward and backward whirls in the rotating frame have been investigated, that is the forward and backward modes are commensurate in the rotating frame. First, the equations for an overhung rotor system with two rotors with coupling stiffness are established by Lagrangian method. By the transformation of a general coordinate system to a rotational coordinate system, we obtained the Campbell diagram in these two coordinate systems. The underlying rotating speeds corresponding to the internal resonances are analyzed by this Campbell diagram in the rotating coordinate system. Accounting for the impact force due to the exceeding of the clearance between the rotor and stator, we applied an ordinary differential equation solver to acquire the solutions, in bifurcation diagrams, orbits, FFT, and spectral density plots. The difference of the current study is investigating the stiffness effects on the nonlinear behaviors. More rich nonlinear phenomena were observed, such as 7:1, 5:1, 4:1, or 3:1 internal resonance in the rotating frame, but quasiperiodic motions are observed in the stationary frame. These internal resonance induced by forward and backward modes in the rotating frame in the FFTs was discussed, which can provide novel explanations for the complicated internal resonance.

title: Boundary mechanisms of externally induced chaos in wind turbine systems under fractional-order damping
abstract: Chaotic behavior in wind turbine systems is fundamentally governed by the interplay between external energy injection and intrinsic dissipation mechanisms, rather than by nonlinearity alone. From this perspective, this study examines how fractional-order damping influences the global dynamical behavior of a nonlinear wind turbine drivetrain while incorporating aerodynamic power capture, maximum power point tracking, and generator-side control. By incorporating the steady torque components into the equilibrium operating point and retaining unequal-amplitude dual-frequency perturbations, the relative torsional dynamics are reformulated via a time-scale transformation as a fractional-order Duffing-type system. Analysis of the unperturbed dynamics shows that under softening-stiffness conditions, the system exhibits a double-well potential with saddle and center equilibria, thereby creating homoclinic orbit structures associated with global chaotic instability. A generalized Melnikov function is derived by treating the two excitation amplitudes as independent parameters, enabling systematic characterization of the combined effects of excitation frequencies, amplitude allocation, nonlinear stiffness, fractional order, and damping intensity on the homoclinic chaos threshold. Numerical investigations based on two- and three-dimensional parameter spaces, bifurcation analysis, attractor geometry, time-domain responses, and spectral characteristics are further performed using the electromechanical model that incorporates maximum power point tracking and control dynamics. The results show that the two excitation components contribute differently to chaos onset, while fractional-order damping significantly shifts the instability threshold and modifies attractor expansion, oscillation intensity, and broadband frequency dispersion. These findings provide a mechanistic insight into drivetrain chaos and quantitative support for torsional instability assessment and parameter selection.

title: Sound-assisted vibration resonance for weak fault detection in machinery
abstract: In nonlinear models, stochastic resonance (SR) is one of the most famous nonlinear phenomena in the past three decades. It completely overturns the traditional concept of “noise is useless”. SR can effectively use the energy of noise to enhance weak signals of interest. Compared with SR, vibration resonance (VR) uses a high-frequency excitation to soften the stiffness of the nonlinear models, change their equilibrium points to bifurcate, thereby enhancing weak useful signals. However, in the field of mechanical weak fault diagnosis, the early naturally developed damage is relatively weak and overwhelmed by a large number of interference frequencies from noise and other signals excited by normal components. In the face of this situation, the traditional VR method that simply uses the high-frequency excitation and vibration signals to enhance weak damage features is not far good enough. Therefore, this paper proposes a method to boost the mechanical weak fault detection by exciting VR using sound-assisted vibration signals. The coupling coefficient is used to control the degree of assistance of the sound signal, and the response amplitude gain is used as an indicator to quantify the weak signal detection performance, so as to improve the weak fault detection capability under extremely low signal-to-noise ratio conditions. Then, the effectiveness of this proposed method is verified by bearing fault experiment. The experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively improve the capability of weak mechanical fault detection. Finally, its superiority is further demonstrated by comparing it with the underdamped time-delay feedback VR method, the classic denoising method and the fast spectral kurtosis method.

title: Nonlinear dynamic behavior and fault diagnosis of rotor-bearing systems subjected to multi-source load unbalance in bulb-type turbine-generator units
abstract: Due to their compact structure and complex hydrodynamic environment, bulb-type turbine-generator units are highly susceptible to multi-source load unbalance rising from hydraulic, electromagnetic, and mechanical interactions, leading to nonlinear vibration behaviors in the rotor-bearing system and posing challenges to stable operation and fault diagnosis. To investigate such dynamics, a nonlinear rotor-bearing dynamic model is first developed based on the Jeffcott rotor theory, incorporating three typical sources of load unbalance: mass eccentricity, angular misalignment, and inadequate oil supply pressure. Nonlinear oil-film forces are modeled to reflect realistic hydrodynamic effects. A dedicated experimental platform is constructed with integrated modules for motor actuation, fault loading, and sensor-based data acquisition. Vibration signals in X and Y directions are collected under varying speeds and fault intensities. A comprehensive analysis using time-domain plots, frequency spectra, orbit diagrams and radar plots reveals distinct fault-specific features. Furthermore, 160 labeled samples across eight rotational speeds are collected, from which 16 time–frequency features are extracted to form a dataset. To enhance fault identification, a Hybrid CNN–Transformer diagnostic model is proposed for the first time in the context of hydropower units. The model integrates convolutional feature extraction with global temporal attention, achieving superior adaptability to varying operating states. Results demonstrate that the model achieves a high classification accuracy of 98.75% on the test set. Confusion matrices show clear decision boundaries, and the average AUC exceeds 0.995, indicating excellent discriminative power. Compared to conventional MLP and LSTM models, the proposed method outperforms in terms of accuracy, robustness, and convergence rate, highlighting its effectiveness and adaptability for fault diagnosis of nonlinear, multi-source load unbalance in bulb-type hydro-turbine units.

title: Nonlinear phenomena, bifurcations, and routes to chaos in an asymmetrically supported rotor–stator contact system
abstract: The efficiency of rotating machines can be improved via precisely manufactured bearings with reduced clearances; consequently, the proclivity for rotor-stator contact is increased. A common model used to investigate rotor-stator contact in previous studies is the two degree-of-freedom (DOF) rotor with symmetric support stiffness, where the contact assumes a linear elastic normal restoring force proportional to the rotor-stator interference and a tangential dry Coulomb friction force. Switching between the contacting and non-contacting states creates strong nonlinearity in the equations of motion, and the dynamic response displays a rich profile of behaviors including periodic, quasiperiodic, and chaotic responses via period-doubling, sudden transitions, quasiperiodicity, and intermittency. For the first time, this work emphasizes an asymmetric support stiffness matrix with cross-coupling between the x and y direction stiffnesses. The influence of support asymmetry on the nonlinear rotor response is shown using rotor orbits, frequency spectra, Poincaré sections, and bifurcation diagrams. It is found that the cross-coupling stiffness coefficient kxy has negligible effect on the dynamic response until its magnitude is on the same order as the direct stiffness coefficients. Direct stiffness coefficient asymmetry is shown to affect the rotor's response, where even small asymmetries can qualitatively change the response. Additionally, the importance of including gravity is investigated, and a method is provided for determining the threshold shaft speed above which gravity can be ignored. The dominant route to chaos is period-doubling for the parameters considered here, though other routes to chaos are seen such as a direct transition from periodic to chaotic motion. Finally, observations pertaining to rotor modeling, design, and fault diagnostics are discussed.

title: A single-parameter multi-stable stochastic resonant nonlinear system with external signal coupled control and its application
abstract: Stochastic resonance (SR) enhances signal detection by exploiting noise. Among the various models, the multi-stable stochastic resonance (MSR) model excels in weak signal detection but requires extensive parameter adjustments. In extremely low signal-to-noise scenarios, parameter adjustments alone are insufficient. This paper simplifies the MSR model into a single-parameter model by analyzing its bifurcation characteristics. Building on this, a coupled-control multi-stable stochastic resonance (CCMSR) system is developed. The steady-state transition laws are analyzed using steady-state probability density (SPD) and mean first-passage time (MFPT). The spectrum amplification (SA) derivation shows that optimal SR effects can be achieved by adjusting the amplitude and frequency of the control signal. Consequently, an adaptive periodic signal-assisted SR method for weak signal detection is proposed. Bearing experiments validate this approach, showing it effectively reduces side-frequency interference in strong background noise and improves weak fault diagnosis in bearings. This offers a novel perspective for enhancing SR output.

title: Nonlinear dynamics study of 4–6 order non-circular planetary gear systems
abstract: Non-circular planetary gear systems exhibit significant time-varying transmission characteristics, which can easily trigger complex nonlinear dynamic responses during operation, adversely affecting vibration stability. This paper develops a 36-degree-of-freedom bending-torsional coupling nonlinear dynamic model for 4–6 order non-circular planetary gear systems, incorporating multiple excitation factors, including time-varying mesh stiffness (TVMS), meshing damping, backlash, friction, and comprehensive transmission error. A TVMS calculation method applicable to both internal and external meshing pairs is proposed based on curvature radius theory. The system’s nonlinear dynamic equations are solved numerically using the Runge-Kutta method. Nonlinear dynamic analyses, including bifurcation diagrams, time histories, phase diagrams, and Poincaré sections, were employed to systematically investigate the influence of key parameters-rotational speed, eccentricity, damping, and backlash on the system response. Multi-scale methods were further used to examine their effects on main resonance characteristics. Quantitative results show that the system transitions from periodic motion to 2-periodic and chaotic states as rotational speed increases, with peak vibration amplitudes rising from 1.12 m/s2 to over 5.6 m/s2 across tested speeds. Eccentricity critically affects dynamic behavior: under identical speed conditions, the external meshing pair enters a quasi-periodic state at an eccentricity of 0.22, earlier than the internal pair at 0.32. Increasing tooth flank clearance can trigger chaotic responses, whereas enhancing system damping reduces peak amplitudes by up to 32%-45%, significantly improving operational stability at medium to high speeds. Finally, a prototype test platform was established to validate the model. Experimental results and theoretical predictions show good agreement, peak to peak comparison has good consistency, confirming that the model effectively captures the system’s main dynamic behavior. These findings elucidate the unique nonlinear dynamics of non-circular planetary gear systems, providing a quantifiable theoretical basis for structural optimization and engineering applications.

title: Nonlinear dynamic modeling and vibration analysis of high-contact-ratio electric drive gear system with multi-source excitation coupling
abstract: To address the issue of local bearing damage in the gear-bearing-housing coupled system of electric drive assemblies for new energy vehicles, this study establishes a coupled dynamic model to investigate the evolution law of nonlinear vibration responses under fault excitation. Firstly, the definition of high contact ratio (HCR) gears is clarified, and gear pairs with total contact ratios of 4.297 and 4.077 are selected to calculate the time-varying friction coefficient (TVFC) and time-varying mesh stiffness (TVMS) of the gears. Secondly, a mathematical model for local bearing failure is constructed and integrated with the gear, leading to the derivation of coupled dynamic equations for the system incorporating a flexible housing. Subsequently, numerical methods are employed to solve the dynamic equations and extract the multi-dimensional dynamic characteristics of the system. Meanwhile, the dependability of the developed model is confirmed by contrasting simulation findings with experimental results, and the underlying mechanism whereby local faults in bearing raceways affect the system vibration response is disclosed. The results reveal that the local defects can cause periodic impact, leading to a significant accumulation of vibration energy at the fault-induced frequency and its harmonics, and induces dense harmonics. Subject to the modulation imposed by the shaft rotary frequency, the fault characteristic frequency associated with the bearing inner ring couples with the gear meshing frequency to constitute combined side frequency bands, and fault excitation gives rise to a distinct enhancement of the sideband amplitudes.

title: Vibration behavior of laminated couplings based on angular misalignment and nonlinear stiffness characteristics
abstract: The coupled bending-torsion vibration model of the laminated coupling was established, taking into account nonlinear stiffness, mass eccentricity, and angular misalignment. First, a laminated coupling vibration test study was conducted. The results showed that the average relative error between the numerical model and the test results was 10.2 %. Subsequently, the effects of the misalignment amount and nonlinear stiffness on the vibration characteristics of the laminated coupling were analyzed. The results showed that an increase in the angular misalignment amount leads to an increase in the vibration amplitude of the laminated coupling. Additionally, nonlinear stiffness has a suppressive effect on the vibration amplitude of the system. Finally, the effects of the angular misalignment amount, bending/torsional stiffness critical values, and rotational speed on the vibration behavior of the laminated coupling were observed using bifurcation diagrams. The research results show that when the angular misalignment exceeds 2.3 × 10−3 rad, the critical value of bending stiffness is greater than 8.44 × 106 N/m, and the critical value of torsional stiffness is lower than 2.88 × 106 N·m/rad, the vibration amplitude of the laminated coupling tends to rise, and resonance may occur. Additionally, controlling the laminated coupling vibration amplitude is more effective when the rotational speed is either in the low-speed range or the high-speed range. The research results detailed in this paper not only inform the design of laminated coupling parameters but also provide guidance for the assembly process.

title: Nonlinear dynamics of rotor-support-casing system with support looseness fault
abstract: This paper proposes a time-domain numerical method combining explicit and implicit schemes for efficiently solving high-dimensional systems with localized nonlinearities. This method is applied to investigate the nonlinear dynamic characteristics of a rotor-support-casing system with support looseness fault. A dynamic model incorporating multi-interface nonlinear supports is developed, which includes nonlinear bearings, a squeeze film damper (SFD), and the contact interaction between the bearing and its housing. The model is validated through modal testing and vibration response experiments. To obtain the vibration response of the system, a hybrid numerical integration method is proposed, with its core focused on optimizing the iterative solution process. This method separates the linear and nonlinear parts of the system, predicts the coupling node response using an explicit scheme, and solves the linear and nonlinear parts using an implicit numerical method and a quasi-Newton iterative algorithm, respectively. Compared with conventional approaches, this method significantly improves computational efficiency. Subsequently, the effects of rotor speed, fit clearance, and oil film clearance in SFD on the dynamic response of the rotor-support-casing system under support looseness faults are investigated. The results show that support looseness alters system stability, leading to periodic, multi-periodic, and quasi-periodic responses. Both fit clearance and oil film clearance significantly influence the system's nonlinear behavior. Under serious fault conditions, fractional-order rotational speed harmonics appear in the casing vibration response. The proposed modeling approach and hybrid numerical method demonstrate strong potential for engineering applications in aero-engine vibration prediction.

title: Global dynamics of a piecewise nonlinear articulated loading platform tower under pitch oscillations in regular sea waves
abstract: Dynamic systems that exhibit piecewise linear or nonlinear characteristics are often strongly nonlinear. Consequently, conventional approaches designed for weakly nonlinear systems may not effectively capture their dynamics, potentially missing critical transitions and leading to incorrect assumptions about stability and performance. The present study investigates the pitch oscillations of a single-degree-of-freedom articulated loading platform tower, influenced by a piecewise nonlinear and asymmetric restoring moment function. By explicitly computing periodic orbits in the frequency domain using the incremental harmonic balance (IHB) method, paired with the Floquet theory for stability analysis, we demonstrate the coexistence of multiple periodic attractors that emerge through period-doubling (PD) routes. Complete mapping of various solution regimes is accomplished by identifying bifurcation points that trigger instabilities in primary and subharmonic resonance branches, leading to chaotic behaviors. Considerable emphasis has been placed on investigating the chaotic dynamics resulting from both supercritical and subcritical flip bifurcations. The basins of attraction offer valuable insights into how the tower responds to changes in initial conditions stemming from diverse marine environments. The study demonstrates that increasing damping to a specific level can effectively quench sub-harmonic resonances and chaotic behaviors.

title: Multi-state dynamics of planetary gear transmission under eccentricity-induced orbiting motion
abstract: Gear eccentricity error critically impacts transmission performance by altering meshing dynamics, thereby reducing system stability and reliability. This study investigates the adverse effects of orbiting motion induced by sun gear (SG) eccentricity on the dynamic behavior of planetary gear transmission (PGT) in wind turbines. A novel multi-state dynamic model of PGT with sun gear eccentricity is developed by incorporating key time-varying meshing parameters, including center distance, tooth contact position, backlash, and meshing stiffness. This model effectively captures the multi-state meshing behavior caused by non-synchronous single-tooth and double-tooth meshes of the internal and external gear pairs in PGT. Results reveal that SG eccentricity severely disturbs these time-varying meshing parameters, thereby intensifying nonlinear vibrations in PGT. The eccentricity amplifies vibration amplitudes and alters motion patterns during tooth disengagement, while its influence diminishes under back-side tooth contact. Increasing parameters like transmission error amplitude and backlash in the presence of SG eccentricity precipitates earlier dynamic instability and bifurcation, implying that smaller tolerances are required for stable operation. Experimental results validate the accuracy and reliability of the proposed model. This work provides critical insights into the failure mechanisms induced by SG eccentricity, offering a theoretical foundation for designing high-reliability wind turbine gearboxes.

title: Axial rubbing-induced nonlinear vibration of shaft-disk system considering base motion
venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation
abstract: In addition to radial rubbing, axial rubbing may also occur between the rotor and stator. However, in recent decades, greater attention has been devoted to the effects of base motion on the radial rubbing of rotating machinery. This paper investigates vibration characteristics induced by axial rubbing in a shaft-disk system considering the influence of base motion. A developed differential equation of motion of the system is proposed, incorporating base motion loads, unbalanced loads, and misalignment loads. The dynamic model is validated by the natural frequencies and measured vibration responses. Subsequently, the dynamic responses are analyzed under different rubbing stiffness, rotating speeds, and base motion speeds. The results indicate that the system with slightly axial rubbing exhibits synchronous periodic motion. In contrast, severe axial rubbing can induce self-excited vibrations and the appearance of frequency near the natural frequencies. Furthermore, base motion excitation is identified as a contributing factor to axial rubbing faults, and phenomena such as the axial collision and rebound are observed. The findings of this study are valuable for vibration control and condition monitoring of rotor systems.

title: From micro-slip to macro-impact: modeling and experimental study on the nonlinear dynamics of a pipeline system during clamp loosening
venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation
abstract: Clamp loosening is a prevalent fault in aero-engine pipeline systems, leading to significant nonlinear vibrations and potential failure due to the transition from micro-slip at friction interfaces to macro-impact between the pipeline and clamp. Despite extensive studies on bolt loosening dynamics, the tribo-dynamic mechanisms underlying clamp loosening, especially throughout the full lifecycle remain poorly understood. This paper presents an integrated experimental and theoretical investigation into the nonlinear vibration response of a pipeline system during progressive clamp loosening. A novel two-scale nonlinear model is developed, combining the LuGre friction model to characterize micro-slip at the bolted interface and a Hertzian contact model with energy loss to represent macro-impact. Four distinct loosening levels are defined based on bolt rotation, and a step-by-step parameter identification method is proposed to calibrate model parameters using measured frequency and time-domain responses. Full-lifecycle vibration tests under both constant frequency and sweep frequency excitations reveal rich nonlinear phenomena, including super-harmonics, sub-harmonics, and chaotic vibrations, with the resonance frequency decreasing nonlinearly as loosening progresses. The simulated responses show excellent agreement with experimental data across all stages, validating the capability of model to capture key nonlinear features induced by clamp loosening. The results provide deep insights into the tribological and dynamic interactions in loosened clamp-pipeline systems and offer a theoretical basis for early fault detection and condition monitoring in high-performance mechanical systems.

title: Effect of internal excitation induced by non-uniform contact of roller bearings on nonlinear vibration and stability of rotor system under combined loads
venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation
abstract: The misalignment of roller bearing rings will results in moment load, together with the unbalance and external loads, forming the combined dynamic loads. The complex combined load can cause non-uniform contact of rollers and rings, which reduces the bearing's life and significantly affect the vibration of rotor systems. This paper mainly studies the roller bearing internal contact performances under combined loads and the influence of internal excitation on the nonlinear vibration of rotor systems. First, the “slices” method is used to establish the mechanical model of roller bearings, which considers the radial clearance and nonlinear Hertz contact. The obtained time-varying bearing nonlinear support reaction is introduced into the rotor concentrated mass model, and a roller bearing–rotor system dynamic model is proposed. Further, the system's complex nonlinear vibrations, such as bifurcation and chaos, are analyzed by spectrum, orbits, bifurcation, and Poincare map. The roller bearing contact performances and stability under the influence of ring tilt angle, rotational speed, and unbalance, are analyzed by contact load statistical features. Finally, based on a rolling bearing–rotor test rig, the vibration experiment considering the combined load was performed, and the experiment results are compared with simulation results to verify the proposed model and conclusions.

title: Complex nonlinear dynamical behaviors of the mechanical vibration system for the cantilever wing plate with variable cross-section: Experiment and theory
abstract: For the nonlinear dynamic characteristics of aircraft structures, the idealized models are often used to simplify the actual structure to reduce the complexity of the analysis and highlight the key response characteristics. The wing is usually modeled as a variable-section wing plate with cantilever boundary conditions, which effectively studied primary structural behaviors in nonlinear vibration. Considering the graphene-reinforced materials, we investigate the complex nonlinear dynamic behaviors of the cantilever wing plate with variable cross-section by using the experiments and theory. The nonlinear vibrational behaviors include the threshold surface, resonance responses, global bifurcations and double-parameter multi-pulse chaotic motions for the system subjected to the parametric and transverse excitations. The vibrational test experiments for the cantilever variable cross section plate are conducted before the theoretical investigation, which the results certify the existence of the complex dynamical behaviors for the mechanical vibration system. For the vibrational theory study of the variable-section wing plate with cantilever boundary conditions, considering the primary resonances, 1/2 sub-harmonic parametric resonances, and the 1:1 internal resonance, the averaged equations for the cantilever variable cross section wing plate are obtained through the multiple scale perturbation (MSP) method. The amplitude-frequency and force-amplitude response curves are depicted to examine the resonant responses. The extended Melnikov method is utilized to evaluate the threshold surface, global bifurcations and double-parameter multi-pulse chaotic dynamics for the system subjected to the parametric and transverse excitations. In the case of the simultaneous resonances, the system exhibits the classical nonlinear hard spring characteristics and two resonance peaks. Under larger parametric or transverse excitations, the nonlinear behavior of the first-order modes for the system becomes more pronounced, resulting in larger resonance peaks. In addition, multi-pulse homoclinic orbits emerge in the system, leading to double-parameter multi-pulse chaotic vibration characteristics under combined the parametric and transverse excitations. Alternating periodic and double-parameter multi-pulse chaotic motions appear for the system in the influence of the parametric and transverse excitations.

title: On the turbulent wake of the actuated fluidic pinball: Dynamics, bifurcations and control authority
abstract: We present the first comprehensive experimental and numerical study featuring the turbulent wake of the fluidic pinball for a large actuation range. The fluidic pinball is a cluster of three equal parallel circular cylinders centered on the vertices of an equilateral triangle, pointing upstream in uniform flow. This configuration has become a canonical benchmark for control-oriented reduced-order modeling, for nonlinear control design and for a large kaleidoscope of drag reduction mechanisms. While the literature covers well the laminar two-dimensional Reynolds number regime, we focus on unexplored terra incognita: experiments of the symmetrically actuated turbulent regime at a Reynolds number of (Formula presented). In other words, the upstream cylinder is kept stationary, while the two downstream cylinders rotate with equal and opposite angular velocities. A large range of base-bleeding and boat-tailing actuation parameters is investigated with time-resolved particle image velocimetry and aerodynamic force measurement with a companion Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes simulation. Our results indicate that the turbulent wake of the fluidic pinball can be approximated by a three-dimensional actuation manifold (Marra et al., 2024 [1]), comprising two inverse pitchfork bifurcations. In the boat-tailing limit, a reduced control authority with a new low-frequency shedding state is observed.

title: Hopf bifurcation analysis and control of actuated wheelset under delayed linear and nonlinear feedback
abstract: This paper investigates the hunting bifurcation behavior of an actuated railway wheelset under delayed linear and nonlinear yaw feedback control. The control force applied by the actuator is described as a delayed polynomial function of the state variables. First, the local stability and the occurrence of Hopf bifurcation are considered by treating the time delay as a bifurcation parameter and analyzing the associated characteristic equation. The explicit formulae are then derived to determine the direction of Hopf bifurcation and the stability of bifurcated periodic solutions using the normal form theory and center manifold theorem. The impact of changes in individual variables on the critical time delay is discussed within a specified range. Finally, the effects of time delay and feedback control gains on the Hopf bifurcation point, type of bifurcation, and limit cycle amplitude are thoroughly examined. Numerical simulations conducted via the continuation package DDE-BIFTOOL validate the theoretical analysis results. Our findings demonstrate that the optimal combination of linear and nonlinear velocity control gains enhances hunting stability by delaying Hopf bifurcation and mitigating hunting oscillations.

title: Self-oscillation of a photo-actuated dual-beam system under linear optical excitation
abstract: Self-oscillating systems utilizing optically responsive liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) are increasingly used in energy harvesting, soft robotics, and actuator applications. However, most studies expose different sections of the same LCE fiber to varying light intensity gradients, leading to local overheating and internal stress concentration, making accurate prediction and control difficult. To overcome these limitations, we propose a dual-beam system operating under a linear optical environment. A general governing equation is formulated, and its asymptotic form is derived for short characteristic times. Numerical analysis reveals a Hopf bifurcation between static and periodic modes. Using multi-scale method, the bifurcation point, oscillation amplitude, and frequency are obtained analytically, and their dependence on system parameters is systematically examined. The analytical solutions agree well with numerical results from both the governing and asymptotic equations, confirming their validity. This system overcomes the limitations of uniform-light models by enabling flexible spatial light regulation, preventing local overheating, and ensuring uniform stress and coordinated deformation. The model is compact and provides a theoretical foundation for analyzing LCE fibers under complex non-uniform or coupled stimulus fields, offering guidance for applications in soft robotics, energy harvesting, and micro-machinery.

title: Chaos and bifurcation in the vibration of a metal cantilever excited by a modulated pulsed laser
abstract: Laser-induced vibration is a promising principle of actuation for its energy conversion from optical to mechanical. The nonlinearity of the optical-thermal-mechanical coupling leads to a narrow drive bandwidth in the high vibration mode and limits its applications to conventional micrometer level. In this study, a mathematical model coupling the photothermal effect and the thermoelastic effect has been derived. The numerical calculation shows that the vibration of the cantilever exhibits chaos, bifurcation and modal interaction as the modulated frequency changes, indicating the potential excitation strategy that we can take advantage of these nonlinear states to enhance the energy efficiency beyond micrometer-scale actuation. We propose a new excitation method to enhance the energy efficiency enabling the generation of millimeter-scale vibrations with a single-point pulsed laser. The nonlinearity of cantilever vibration can be further enhanced by controlling the pulse laser frequency, driving the system from stable state to chaos and bifurcation, which leads to increased amplitude and energy efficiency. Compared to stable state, chaos and bifurcation can amplify the amplitude of the cantilever by 5 to 10 times, respectively, with a maximum amplitude of 0.69 mm and 2.31 mm in experimental validations. This allows the laser induced excitation to offer the potential for widely using in non-destructive testing, precision operations, and driving micro-resonators.

title: Pitchfork bifurcation of symmetric periodic oscillations in comb-drive finger MEMS
venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation
abstract: This paper presents the first analytical investigation of nontrivial even periodic solutions arising through local pitchfork bifurcations in a cubic comb-drive MEMS model subjected to a non-constant, even, periodic voltage excitation Vλ (t). The governing equation is a second-order nonlinear oscillator with cubic stiffness and electrostatic forcing. Using Sturm–Liouville spectral theory, oscillation theory for Hill equations, and bifurcation analysis, we prove that pitchfork bifurcations occur at a finite sequence of parameter values λ , corresponding to spectral values of an associated Sturm–Liouville problem. We establish the existence of families of even periodic solutions with prescribed nodal properties bifurcating from the trivial equilibrium x ≡ 0, and show that these bifurcations are subcritical and accompanied by local stability changes. The analysis is carried out for an idealized undamped model that preserves the underlying symmetries. Numerical simulations based on high-order Taylor integration confirm the theoretical predictions and accurately locate the bifurcation values. Additional simulations with linear damping indicate convergence to the equilibrium state for typical MEMS damping levels, while sufficiently small damping preserves dynamics close to the undamped regime. This work provides a theoretical characterization of pitchfork bifurcations in cubic comb-drive MEMS oscillators and could serve as a first step toward more realistic studies that include damping.

title: Flutter suppression and bifurcation reconfiguration of an airfoil using pre-stressed nonlinear vibration absorbers
abstract: Passive flutter suppression requires absorbers that can improve the local stability boundary while regulating nonlinear post-flutter responses. This study investigates pre-stressed nonlinear vibration absorbers attached to a two-dimensional typical airfoil section with a control surface, focusing on pre-compression and pre-tension configurations. A coupled aeroelastic model based on Theodorsen’s unsteady aerodynamic theory is developed, and time-domain simulations, two-parameter bifurcation analysis, numerical continuation, Hilbert-Huang analysis, and energy analysis are combined to examine flutter onset, bifurcation reconfiguration, resonance capture, and energy dissipation. The two-parameter analysis reveals that Hopf-Hopf bifurcations organize the interaction between Neimark-Sacker and cyclic-fold curves, thereby governing the transition between low-amplitude modulated responses and fold-induced large-amplitude oscillations. The results show that pre-stress introduces a tunable equivalent linear stiffness, enabling both absorber configurations to modify the flutter boundary. However, their nonlinear post-flutter behaviors differ substantially. Within the investigated parameter range, the pre-tension absorber produces a more favorable bifurcation structure by separating the low-amplitude response path from the large-amplitude branch and delaying the jump boundary. Time-frequency and energy analyses further show intermittent resonance capture and directed transfer of aerodynamic energy into absorber damping, with limited energy backflow when the absorber is properly tuned. Compared with the classical nonlinear energy sink under the examined conditions, the tuned pre-tension nonlinear vibration absorber increases the Hopf onset speed, delays the jump boundary, and substantially reduces the post-flutter response amplitude. These findings indicate that pre-tension nonlinear vibration absorbers provide a promising passive strategy for flutter suppression through the combined regulation of bifurcation structure and energy dissipation.

title: Dynamics characteristic analysis of rudder actuator with lubrication clearance under transient impact load
abstract: In previous dynamic analyses of rudder actuator with clearance, it was typically assumed that the linkages were rigid, and the lubrication of the revolute joints was overlooked. However, the introduction of lubrication clearance and flexible linkage significantly alters the dynamic response of the mechanism. Given that the rudder actuator is influenced by practical factors such as lubrication clearance, flexible linkages, and impact loads on the rudder surface, this work constructs a dynamic model with rigid-flexible coupling to characterize the behavior of the rudder actuator under lubrication clearance conditions. This model is based on an improved hybrid contact force model, integrated with a modified Pinkus-Sternlicht model and a flexible beam element model. The analysis assessed the effects of various different nonlinear influences on the system’s dynamic performance and its nonlinear attributes. The findings indicated that linkage flexibility exacerbates the system's chaos behavior, whereas lubricants effectively alleviate this issue. However, lubricants are unable to reduce the chaos behavior of the mechanism with excessively small clearances. Additionally, it is observed that transient impact loads intensify the system's dynamic response and have a persistent impact on subsequent cycles. Finally, experiments validate the effectiveness of the theoretical model. This study provides a theoretical foundation for accurately analyzing the dynamic characteristics of rudder actuators with clearance and supports the precise control of such mechanisms.

title: Semi-automated design strategy for multi-stable magnetic out-of-plane actuators with accurate pre-defined positions
abstract: This work presents an analytical modeling approach for the semi-automated design of magnetic actuators with multiple pre-defined stable positions. The analyzed system allows for large out-of-plane displacements of a freely movable permanent magnetic plunger that is actuated by electromagnetic coils for switching between multiple stable resting positions, in which the plunger can be held without the need for further continuous energy consumption. These equilibrium positions are generated by the reluctance force between several mu-metal rings and the permanent magnet. Instead of computationally expensive finite element modeling, a phenomenological model is derived that describes the force contribution of single mu-metal rings depending on their dimensions. We exploit this analytical computation to accurately describe arbitrary multi-ring configurations, enabling an efficient analysis and design procedure. This model then provides the foundation for a requirements-driven design approach, in which pre-defined stable positions are used to derive the corresponding mu-metal ring configuration. In this context, the robustness of the system in terms of force barriers between the stable states is also considered. This eventually enables an automated design process that significantly reduces the complexity compared to manually designing application-specific setups. The modeling and design approaches are validated experimentally, showing good agreement between the predicted and measured force-displacement curves.

title: Vibration suppression analysis of active magnetic bearing systems considering time-delay bifurcation and amplitude jump
abstract: This work investigates resonance instability and vibration suppression in active magnetic bearing (AMB) systems, with particular attention to the coupled effects of time-delay bifurcation and amplitude jump phenomena. The influences of proportional-derivative (PD) feedback gains and control-loop delays on the equivalent damping and nonlinear stiffness of the AMB system are examined. Hassard's stability criterion is employed to determine the allowable stable delay regions, and the corresponding boundaries are identified as Hopf bifurcation points via the transversality condition and root locus analysis. The stiffness hardening-softening transition of active magnetic bearings is identified via cubic nonlinear‑stiffness coefficients, and the analytical results obtained from the improved multiple‑scale method are used to verify this transition mechanism under external excitation and to explore the amplitude–frequency characteristics. The Routh–Hurwitz criterion is then applied to determine the amplitude jump regions, and a joint analysis of the jump regions and Hassard stable domains is performed to evaluate the overall resonance stability. The coupling effects of control gains, time delays, and external excitation on resonance stability are summarized and validated through numerical simulations and experiments. Results show that mismatched feedback gains broaden the resonance range, aggravate amplitude jumps, and ultimately induce Hopf bifurcation. The critical delays of the displacement and velocity channels exhibit an opposite evolution trend with varying velocity feedback gain, whereas the displacement feedback gain governs the evolution of stiffness from hardening to softening. Setting the displacement gain near the boundary of the jump region enables a trade-off between low resonant amplitude and favorable stability margins. Experimental results corroborate the theoretical predictions and simulations regarding amplitude jump evolution and Hopf bifurcation, and further confirm the effectiveness of the proposed vibration suppression strategy.

title: Approximate analytical solutions of nonlinear vibration and bifurcation of dielectric elastomer balloon
abstract: Dielectric elastomers (DE), a novel class of actuators, are increasingly employed in fields such as soft robotics and vibration control. Most existing studies investigating the dynamic characteristics of DE structures neglect the viscoelasticity and strain-stiffening effects of materials, with only a few offering approximate analytical solutions. This paper establishes the governing equation for the dynamics of a DE balloon, utilizing the principle of virtual work and considering material viscoelasticity and strain-stiffening effects through linear damping and the Gent hyperelastic model, respectively. The nonlinear governing equations are simplified using the Chebyshev polynomial approximation. The multiple scales method is applied to derive approximate solutions for the structure's free vibration under static voltage excitation and parametrically excited vibration under harmonic voltage excitation. The accuracy of these approximate analytical solutions is validated by comparison with numerical solutions. Additionally, the paper analyzes stability and bifurcation phenomena through time-domain response curves, amplitude-frequency curves, and phase trajectories. Furthermore, the influence of the stretching limit, voltage, and damping on the nonlinear vibration of the balloon structure is studied, providing a valuable theoretical foundation for the future design and utilization of dielectric elastomers.

title: Stochastic bifurcation and chaotic dynamics of viscoelastic von Mises truss under harmonic excitation with time-delayed feedback control
venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation
abstract: This paper investigates the nonlinear stochastic dynamics of a viscoelastic von Mises truss under harmonic excitation, time-delayed feedback control, and Gaussian white noise, using a standard linear solid model to capture energy dissipation and material memory effects. By combining the stochastic center manifold theorem and stochastic averaging method, the high-dimensional system is reduced to an amplitude-governed stochastic differential equation, from which the stationary probability density is derived to analyze stochastic bifurcation. The stochastic Melnikov method is further applied to establish the mean-square threshold for chaotic motion. Results show that variations in system parameters alter the stationary probability density, indicating a shift in the most probable response state; noise intensity reduces the chaos threshold, while an appropriate time delay can increase it and delay chaos onset. Numerical simulations, including bifurcation diagrams and Lyapunov exponents, validate the theoretical predictions.

title: Rigid-flexible coupling modeling and nonlinear analysis of rudder actuator with lubrication clearance
abstract: To investigate the coupling effects of clearance and flexible components on dynamic performance of pushrod-driven actuator, this study proposes a hybrid contact force model suitable for large loads with an adaptive restitution coefficient, and a modified transitional lubrication force model. Considering the influence of flexible components, a rigid-flexible coupling dynamics model of the actuator incorporating lubrication clearance is established. Subsequently, effects of clearance size, driving speed, dynamic viscosity and load on system's dynamics and chaos are then analyzed. Finally, experimental validation confirms the model's effectiveness. The results show that the choice of clearance size and drive speed significantly influences system stability, and that high dynamic viscosity lubricants can lower the output vibration frequency and amplitude. Under large loads, the lubricant film thickness at clearance approaches zero, intensifying clearance collisions and wear. This increases the output vibration frequency, and substantially reduces the lubricant's mitigating effects on clearance and flexible factors. This study provides theoretical support for the design of high-performance rudder actuators.

title: Experimental research on supersonic shock wave/boundary layer interaction controlled by alternating continuous plasma actuation
abstract: A pulsed arc plasma alternating continuous discharge circuit was designed to control supersonic shock wave/boundary layer interaction (SWBLI). By controlling the on and off states of the electronic switches in the charging circuit, it enables the integration of high-frequency actuation and high-energy actuation, overcoming the traditional limitation that high energy and high frequency cannot be achieved simultaneously. Using a high-speed schlieren system and surface fluorescent oil-flow visualization, the evolution of the flow-field shock system structure and the wall-surface separation region were captured. The results indicate that, for shock wave system control, the actuation frequency is a key factor influencing the control effectiveness. On the one hand, plasma actuation continuously affects the shock wave structure, intensifying its unsteadiness and reducing the shock angle. On the other hand, actuation mitigates the low-frequency instability of the shock wave, increasing the proportion of high-frequency components dominated by the actuation frequency. For separation-region control, a "W"-shaped separation line forms at an actuation frequency of 10 kHz. The separation point downstream of the actuation location moves upstream, while the separation points on both sides move downstream, resulting in a net downstream shift of the mean separation line. This phenomenon is related to the evolution of vortex structures induced by actuation. Under the premise of effective shock wave system control, separation regulation results from a trade-off between actuation frequency and actuation energy. This study provides new control concepts and methodological support for the regulation of shock wave/boundary layer interaction and flow separation control in supersonic aircraft.

title: Experimental and computational study of pMDI aerosol delivery in mucus-coated pediatric airways: Effects of inhalation flow and actuation timing
abstract: This study investigates airflow and aerosol deposition in a pediatric mouth–throat (MT) airway model by integrating a cystic fibrosis (CF) inhalation profile, pressurized metered-dose inhaler (pMDI) actuation timing, and an artificial mucus layer to improve understanding of aerosol drug delivery mechanisms. A computed tomography–derived pediatric MT airway model was three-dimensionally printed and coated with artificial pulmonary mucus, establishing a physiologically relevant baseline to assess the effects of a non-Newtonian, shear-thinning mucus layer on drug deposition. The geometry was subsequently integrated into a Next Generation Impactor (NGI) for experimental validation of the computational fluid dynamics framework. The Eulerian wall film (EWF) approach was employed to model the mucus layer, while large-eddy simulation (LES) and discrete-phase modeling (DPM) were used to analyze airflow and particle transport, respectively. Results indicate that inhalation flow rate is the primary determinant of deposition efficiency, with Morris sensitivity analysis showing a strong correlation (rₛ = 0.81). Higher inhalation flow rates increased wall shear stress, thereby enhancing shear-driven particle transport. The presence of shear-thinning mucus modified flow structures by altering secondary flow patterns, inducing asymmetric swirling, and increasing the minimum particle size exiting the trachea by 60.2% (from 0.491 to 0.789 µm) compared with Newtonian mucus. Actuation timing also played a secondary influence on regional deposition, with synchronized pMDI actuation achieving the highest delivery efficiency (approximately 46%) due to improved aerosol entrainment during the acceleration phase of the CF inhalation profile.

title: Analyzing stability and bifurcation of a controlled dynamical system: A comparative study of negative velocity feedback and positive position feedback controllers
abstract: In order to determine how well two sophisticated control techniques—negative velocity feedback (NVFB) and positive position feedback (PPF)—can regulate the dynamic behavior of the Van der Pol-Duffing-Helmholtz nonlinear oscillator, this paper offers a fresh analysis of them. The multiple-scales approach (MSA), which was chosen for its accuracy in handling nonlinear dynamics, will be used to solve each technique after it has been developed independently. In addition, stability will be investigated using the Routh-Hurwitz criteria (RHC), as well as the basin of attraction based on the largest Lyapunov exponent (LLE), phase portraits, Poincaré maps, and bifurcation events. Additionally, parametric experiments will show how vital factors affect amplitude response, providing information for improving control performance. It is expected that these results will offer practical answers to real-world engineering problems, such as improving energy harvesting or controlling vibration in aircraft. Additionally, by reducing noise in car suspension systems, these solutions improved passenger comfort and increased the precision of robotic systems in industrial automation.

title: Non-smooth bifurcation structures and chaos control in a quarter-car piecewise-linear suspension system with time-delayed velocity feedback
abstract: Advanced vehicle suspension systems often incorporate piecewise-smooth and non-smooth stiffness and damping elements, making them susceptible to complex nonlinear behaviors, including multi-periodicity, bifurcations, and chaos, particularly under parametric uncertainties and external excitations. Such dynamics can degrade ride comfort, accelerate structural wear, and jeopardize operational safety, underscoring the necessity for precise dynamical characterization and effective control strategies. In this study, the bifurcation structure and chaos suppression of a harmonically excited quarter-car piecewise-linear suspension (QC-PLS) are systematically investigated using time-delayed velocity feedback control. Complex periodic responses of both uncontrolled and controlled systems are computed in the frequency domain via the incremental harmonic balance (IHB) method, while their stability is evaluated with a semi-discretization-based Floquet framework. The uncontrolled QC-PLS system exhibits rich nonlinear dynamics, including multiple coexisting primary and subharmonic resonance branches, simultaneous subcritical and supercritical flip bifurcations, and broadband chaotic responses stemming from mixed-mode period-doubling cascades. To mitigate these adverse behaviors, delayed linear and nonlinear velocity feedback controllers are designed within the IHB framework—an approach that remains largely unexplored for non-smooth systems. Controller gains and delay parameters are selected based on local equilibrium stability criteria. The proposed control strategies effectively suppress higher-order subharmonic resonances, flip bifurcations, and chaotic oscillations, guiding the system toward stable, low-amplitude periodic responses. For identical control parameters, pure linear velocity feedback is found to outperform purely nonlinear feedback in terms of vibration attenuation and stability enhancement. Bifurcation diagrams and basins of attraction further reveal that substantially larger negative velocity gains are necessary to eliminate strong chaotic motions compared to weak chaos. The analytical predictions are corroborated by direct time-domain numerical simulations (NS), confirming the accuracy of the IHB-based analysis and the robustness of the proposed control schemes. The work provides a comprehensive theoretical and computational framework for analysing and controlling non-smooth quarter-car suspension systems that exhibit complex nonlinear dynamics.

title: Manipulation of liquid transport and droplet switch using light-actuated surface tension
venue: Colloids and Surfaces A: Physicochemical and Engineering Aspects
abstract: The manipulation of microfluidic systems plays a crucial role in various applications within biology, chemistry, and materials science. However, conventional driving techniques often involve complex setups or rely on external forces, which limits their potential for miniaturization and integration. In this study, we propose a novel method for manipulating microfluidic systems using an azobenzene photosensitive surfactant stimulated by light. This approach offers a simpler and more convenient alternative for controlling microfluidic devices. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our light-driven method, we apply it to control the transition between two bifurcations in a double droplet system (DDS) by surpassing its surface energy barrier. Experimental results demonstrate successful transitions between the bifurcations of the DDS using the light-driven approach. To gain a deeper understanding of the transition process, we establish a dynamic model that considers the surfactant absorption process during the experiment. Furthermore, we provide a simple application of the proposed driving method through a light-activated tunable liquid lens, demonstrating its potential for broader applications in microfluidic systems. This work is expected to contribute to the development of novel light-driven microfluidic manipulation techniques.

title: Bifurcation-gated kresling origami triboelectric mechanoreceptor enabling self-powered multimodal tactile sensing for intelligent human-robot interaction
abstract: Tactile sensors play major roles in human-robot interaction (HRI) by providing essential feedback on physical stimuli. In this context, bio-inspired design offers a promising route to reproducing the adaptive and multimodal sensing functions of biological tactile systems. Within this biomimetic framework, human-like tactile perception can be achieved by emulating the complementary dual-sensing behaviors of cutaneous mechanoreceptors, comprising Fast-Adaptive (FA) receptors responding to dynamic stimuli, and Slow-Adaptive (SA) receptors producing sustained responses to static stimuli. While triboelectric tactile sensors serve as substantial solutions, their sensing capability is primarily optimized for dynamic motion. In this study, we introduce a bifurcation-gated sensing strategy embodied in a Bio-inspired Origami-based Triboelectric mechanoreceptor (BOT) that discriminates between dynamic and static stimuli through a single compliant structure. The Kresling origami of the BOT exhibits a kinematic bifurcation at a buckling threshold. Below this threshold, dynamic loads produce FA mode, whereas static loads exceeding the threshold activate a SA mode that generates sustained signals during deformation. The BOT achieves highly linear sensing of indentation depth and normal force. Its practical utility is demonstrated through a self-powered collision detection system for safety and a deep learning-based material recognition framework capable of identifying properties under electromagnetic interference (EMI) environments. This work establishes the bifurcation-gated design principle as an alternative to multi-mechanism, opening a pathway toward triboelectric tactile sensors with mechanical property perception for HRI systems.

title: Aeroelastic analysis of moving mass actuated UAV wing
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) relying on conventional external control surfaces, for attitude and trim control, often exhibit reduced aerodynamic efficiency. Moving Mass Control (MMC) which relies on moving a mass block inside the wing structure has emerged as a promising alternative to external control surfaces for attitude and trim control. Existing studies on MMC predominantly focus on flight dynamics and control applications, and evaluate the aeroelastic performance by considering the moving mass as a quasi-static process. However, the moving mass can induce significant time-varying dynamical effects on the aeroelastic behaviour compared to quasi-static assumption. Therefore, this study investigates the effects of moving mass induced time-varying dynamics on the aeroelastic response and stability of an MMC-equipped UAV wing. The aeroelastic equations of motion are derived using Lagrange’s equation and modified Renaudot formulation, considering the coupling between structural dynamics, unsteady aerodynamics and the moving mass-induced dynamics. The resulting aeroelastic equations are found to be characterised by time-varying inertia, pseudo-damping and stiffness matrices arising from prescribed mass kinematics, which are numerically integrated in the time domain to obtain the aeroelastic responses. For aeroelastic stability analysis of the MMC wing, the traditional eigenvalue-based flutter analysis is not applicable, as the aeroelastic equations of the MMC wing have time-varying coefficients in addition to aerodynamic matrices dependent on varying airspeed. Hence, a Floquet-theory-based aeroelastic stability analysis is proposed to predict flutter in MMC wings which accounts for inherent time-varying system dynamics. This approach requires computation of the monodromy matrix of the full state-space system over one actuation period for each flight speed. Numerical results show that MMC can effectively enhance aeroelastic stability by delaying flutter onset. The results further reveal that mass placement and actuation speed are critical design parameters governing system stability and response. These findings establish MMC as an effective flutter suppression mechanism, in addition to attitude and trim control, offering new design opportunities for advanced UAV configurations.

title: Fuzzy prescribed performance backstepping control for ship roll chaotic motion under actuator faults
abstract: To address the problem of chaos suppression in ship roll motion under actuator faults and to enhance control performance and navigation safety under faulty conditions, a fixed-time prescribed performance backstepping control method based on a fuzzy state observer is proposed By designing a fixed-time prescribed performance function, the dynamic performance of the tracking error is strictly constrained; a fuzzy state observer is constructed to estimate unknown system states in real time; and a fuzzy logic system is introduced to approximate the unknown nonlinear functions arising from actuator faults and model uncertainties. Through the Lyapunov theorem, the semi-global uniform ultimate bounded (SGUUB) properties of the proposed control algorithm are proved. Finally, simulations verify that the proposed method can effectively suppress chaotic phenomena in ship rolling motion under actuator failures, ensure rapid convergence within a fixed time, and comply with the prescribed dynamic performance requirements. This approach significantly improves the system’s convergence speed, robustness, and fault tolerance.

title: Minimal actuation and control of a soft hydrogel swimmer from flutter instability
venue: Journal of the Mechanics and Physics of Solids
abstract: Micro-organisms propel themselves in viscous environments by the periodic, nonreciprocal beating of slender appendages known as flagella. Active materials have been widely exploited to mimic this form of locomotion. However, the realization of such coordinated beating in biomimetic flagella requires complex actuation modulated in space and time. We prove through experiments on polyelectrolyte hydrogel samples that directed undulatory locomotion of a soft robotic swimmer can be achieved by untethered actuation from a uniform and static electric field. A minimal mathematical model is sufficient to reproduce, and thus explain, the observed behavior. The periodic beating of the swimming hydrogel robot emerges from flutter instability thanks to the interplay between its active and passive reconfigurations in the viscous environment. Interestingly, the flutter-driven soft robot exhibits a form of electrotaxis whereby its swimming trajectory can be controlled by simply reorienting the electric field. Our findings trace the route for the embodiment of mechanical intelligence in soft robotic systems by the exploitation of flutter instability to achieve complex functional responses to simple stimuli. While the experimental study is conducted on millimeter-scale hydrogel swimmers, the design principle we introduce requires simple geometry and is hence amenable for miniaturization via micro-fabrication techniques. We believe it may also be transferred to a wider class of soft active materials.

title: Piezoelectric air actuators for electronic thermal management: a bibliometric and comprehensive review
abstract: With the continuous rise in heat flux density in high-power electronic devices, conventional cooling strategies increasingly struggle to achieve an effective balance among system footprint, noise, energy consumption, and heat transfer performance. Piezoelectric air actuators have therefore emerged as a promising active air-cooling technology for electronic thermal management. This review examines 660 relevant publications indexed in the Web of Science from 2000 to 2026, identified through topic-based screening and citation tracing. The bibliometric analysis systematically examines the field's developmental trajectory, research collaboration networks, and evolving research hotspots. The technical analysis also comprehensively and critically examines the structural evolution, flow mechanisms, and heat transfer characteristics of cantilever-type piezoelectric fans, zero-net-mass-flux piezoelectric synthetic jet actuators, and non-zero-net-mass-flux piezoelectric synthetic jet actuators. A complete energy-transfer chain from electrical input to heat removal is established, and a multidimensional evaluation framework integrating flow, thermal, and acoustic performance is further proposed. By linking academic advances with industrial practice, this review indicates that ultrasonic-frequency piezoelectric synthetic jet actuators may offer application-specific advantages for high-heat-flux, low-noise, thin, array-scalable, and embedded electronic cooling systems. Finally, current limitations include insufficient understanding of multiphysics coupling, inadequate system-level evaluation criteria, limited array coordination, and inadequate operational stability. Commercialization is further constrained by manufacturing repeatability and system-level competitiveness. Future research should prioritize energy efficiency, long-term reliability, and versatile applicability, providing theoretical guidance for the development of compact piezoelectric active air-cooling technologies.

title: Inverse kinematic analysis and agile control of a magnetically actuated catheter
abstract: In recent years, there has been a growing application of robotic-assisted magnetic actuation systems in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases because of the fast response and the miniaturization of medical tools. However, inverse kinematic (IK) modeling in permanent magnet systems is still a challenging task due to the complexity of the magneto-solid strong coupling field. In this paper, we present a magnetic actuation system that uses the rotation of a single permanent magnet to steer the intravascular catheter. The main contribution is the proposal of an IK modeling method that establishes a relationship between the catheter's deflection angle and the rotation angle of the driving magnet (DM). Our proposed method uses the constant curvature model (CCM) to decouple the catheter's deformation and the magnetic loads, thus enabling the efficient estimation of the position of the catheter's tip based on the desired deflection angle. After establishing the equilibrium equation, we employ a numerical computation method to optimize the rotation angle of the DM. To facilitate fast convergence, we propose an analytical solution to determine the optimal initial value. Our proposed IK modeling method has been proven to be effective in the model validation experiment, which achieves a good balance between accuracy and efficiency. The difference between the planned and actual deflection angle is 4.55±3.44° and the distal position error is 1.26±0.74 mm. The completion time of our IK method is 1–4 ms. The performance of our magnetic actuation system has been evaluated in the phantom experiment, in which the catheter can pass sequentially through the planned bifurcations and finally reach all the goals under the magnetic guidance.

title: Numerical bifurcation analysis of post-contact states in mathematical models of Micro-Electromechanical Systems
abstract: This paper is a computational bifurcation analysis of a non-linear partial differential equation (PDE) characterizing equilibrium configurations in Micro electromechanical Systems (MEMS). MEMS are engineering systems that utilize electrostatic forces to actuate elastic surfaces. The potential equilibrium states of MEMS are described by solutions of a singularly perturbed elliptic nonlinear PDE. We develop a numerical method which couples a finite element approximation with mesh refinement to a pseudo arc-length continuation algorithm to numerically obtain bifurcation diagrams in the physically relevant two dimensional scenario. Several geometries, including a unit disk, square, and annulus, are studied to understand the behavior of the system over a range of domains and parameter regimes. We find that solution multiplicity, and importantly the potential for bistability in the system, depends sensitively on the parameters. In the annulus domain, symmetry breaking bifurcations are located and asymmetric solution branches are tracked. This work significantly extends the envelope for numerical characterization of equilibrium states in microscopic electrostatic contact problems relating to MEMS.

title: Nonlinear hydrodynamics and dynamic softening of MFC-actuated underwater flexible structure
abstract: Piezoelectric flexible structures are pivotal for underwater bionic propulsion due to their compact form and high agility. This study investigates the nonlinear hydrodynamics and resonant behaviors of flexible beams internally actuated by macro fiber composites (MFC) in viscous fluids. A dynamic model is established, coupling the internal bending moment generated by the MFC with the external hydrodynamic loading. Comprehensive 2D computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations are performed to elucidate the flow evolution from linear viscous diffusion to nonlinear convection as the structural vibration amplitude increases. CFD simulations reveal that the shedding of energetic vortices at finite amplitudes drives a strong hydrodynamic nonlinearity, specifically manifesting as enhanced fluid damping. Consequently, a modified semi-analytical hydrodynamic function, characterized by an amplitude-dependent nonlinear damping term, is derived to correct the fluid forces. Comprehensive experiments are conducted to examine the resonant behaviors of the structure under varying driving voltages. The variations of the underwater natural frequency, quality factor, and frequency response behavior are analyzed. Experimental results uncover a distinct dynamic softening effect: the fundamental resonant frequency shifts from 4.46 Hz to 3.45 Hz, a 22.6% reduction, as the vibration amplitude increases. This frequency attenuation arises from the coupled effects of frequency-dependent added mass and amplitude-dependent nonlinear hydrodynamic damping.
